laws.title: Alcohol Sales Restrictions
laws.subtitle: Law 4250 — No alcohol sales 10pm–6am
laws.fullDescription: Turkey bans alcohol sales between 10pm and 6am. Alcohol is banned within 100 metres of educational and religious buildings. Despite being a predominantly Muslim country, alcohol is legal but increasingly restricted. Some areas with high tourist traffic have specific rules.
laws.penalty: Businesses selling alcohol outside permitted hours: fines up to ₺50,000 + licence suspension.
exceptions: Licensed hotels may serve to guests at all hours
Duty-free purchases

quiz.q: When are alcohol sales banned in Turkey?
quiz.explanation: Turkey bans alcohol sales from 10pm to 6am.

laws.title: Turkish Hospitality — Tea and Warmth are Compulsory
laws.subtitle: Çay (tea) is social currency; never refuse it
laws.fullDescription: Turkish hospitality revolves around çay (black tea). Refusing tea when offered is considered very impolite — always accept at least one glass. Greetings involve handshakes; close friends may embrace warmly. Remove shoes before entering homes. Older people are addressed formally (Bey/Hanım after the first name, e.g. 'Ahmet Bey'). When visiting a mosque, dress modestly and remove shoes.
laws.penalty: No legal penalty — refusing tea or hospitality is a social faux pas.
exceptions: Major tourist/business areas more forgiving of Western norms
Younger urban generation more casual

quiz.q: What should you always do when offered çay (tea) in Turkey?
options: Ask what type it is first
quiz.explanation: Refusing Turkish tea (çay) when offered is considered impolite — always accept at least one glass.

laws.title: Insulting the President — Criminal Offence
laws.subtitle: Turkish Penal Code Art. 299 — Up to 4 years imprisonment
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Article 299 of the Turkish Penal Code makes insulting the President a criminal offence carrying up to 4 years imprisonment. Social media posts, cartoons, and criticism of the President can and have led to prosecutions of both Turkish citizens and foreigners. Tens of thousands of cases have been filed since 2014. Insult of 'Turkishness' (Art. 301) is a separate offence.
laws.penalty: Insulting the President (Art. 299): 1–4 years imprisonment. Insulting Turkishness (Art. 301): 6 months to 2 years.
exceptions: Some forms of political criticism defended as free speech — inconsistently applied
Foreign press coverage given some tolerance

quiz.q: What is Article 299 of the Turkish Penal Code?
options: Law against insulting the President (up to 4 years)
quiz.explanation: Turkish Penal Code Art. 299 criminalises insulting the President — tens of thousands of cases have been filed since 2014, including against social media users.

laws.title: Social Media Platform Bans — Repeated Restrictions
laws.subtitle: Law 7253 (2020) — Platforms must appoint local representative
laws.fullDescription: Turkey regularly bans or throttles social media platforms (Twitter/X, Wikipedia was banned 2017–2020, TikTok temporarily). Law 7253 (2020) requires platforms with over 1 million daily users to appoint a local representative and comply with data removal requests or face advertising bans and bandwidth throttling up to 90%. VPNs are widely used but not officially endorsed.
laws.penalty: Non-compliant platforms: up to 90% bandwidth reduction and advertising ban. Content non-removal: fines up to ₺40 million.
exceptions: Diplomatic communications
Verified news organisations (limited)

quiz.q: Which major website was banned in Turkey from 2017 to 2020?
quiz.explanation: Wikipedia was banned in Turkey from 2017 to 2020 under Law 5651 — Turkey has a history of temporarily blocking major platforms.

laws.title: Cappadocia — Hot Air Balloon Safety and Heritage Rules
laws.subtitle: SHGM — Licensed operators only; UNESCO-adjacent protection
laws.fullDescription: Cappadocia's famous hot air balloon flights over the fairy chimneys are one of Turkey's top tourist attractions. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (SHGM) strictly regulates all balloon operators — only licensed operators may fly. Unlicensed or unsafe operators have caused fatal accidents. Balloon flights are weather-dependent and can be cancelled — reputable operators will not fly in unsafe conditions. The Göreme National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site) has rules against damaging the volcanic rock formations (peri bacaları). Rock climbing on the fairy chimneys requires permits.
laws.penalty: Operating unlicensed balloon: criminal offence + grounding. Damaging fairy chimneys: fine + criminal charges under heritage law.
exceptions: Licensed SHGM-certified balloon operators
Authorised climbing companies with Göreme National Park permits
laws.sourceLabel: SHGM — Turkish Directorate General of Civil Aviation

quiz.q: What must Cappadocia hot air balloon operators have to fly legally?
options: SHGM (Civil Aviation) certification — unlicensed operators are criminal
quiz.explanation: All Cappadocia balloon operators must have SHGM (Civil Aviation) certification — unlicensed operators have caused fatal accidents and their operation is a criminal offence.

laws.title: Article 301 — Insulting 'Turkishness' Is a Criminal Offence
laws.subtitle: Turkish Penal Code Art. 301 — Up to 2 years for insulting Turkish identity
laws.fullDescription: Article 301 of the Turkish Penal Code makes it a criminal offence to publicly denigrate 'the Turkish Nation', the Republic of Turkey, or its state institutions. The law was introduced in 2005 (replacing the older Article 159) and controversially amended in 2008 to require the Justice Minister's approval before prosecutions can proceed — a safeguard intended to reduce abuse but which has not eliminated cases. High-profile prosecutions under Article 301 and its predecessor include Nobel Prize-winning novelist Orhan Pamuk (for stating that 30,000 Kurds and one million Armenians were killed in Turkey), and journalist Elif Şafak. The law is frequently criticised by the European Union as incompatible with freedom of expression standards, and it has complicated Turkey's EU accession process. Even foreign nationals can face prosecution if the alleged offence occurs on Turkish soil or targets Turkish institutions.
laws.penalty: Insulting the Turkish Nation or Republic of Turkey: 6 months to 2 years imprisonment. If the offence is committed by a Turkish citizen abroad: penalty increased by one-third.
exceptions: Prosecution requires the Justice Minister's written approval (since 2008 amendment) — intended to reduce political abuse
Academic and journalistic work framed as objective criticism has sometimes been acquitted, though inconsistently
laws.sourceLabel: Turkish Penal Code Art. 301 — Mevzuat (Official Legislation)

quiz.q: Why was Nobel Prize-winning Turkish author Orhan Pamuk prosecuted under Turkish law in 2005?
options: For writing about the Ottoman Empire
For stating in a Swiss newspaper interview that 30,000 Kurds and one million Armenians were killed in Turkey
For criticising the Turkish education system
quiz.explanation: Orhan Pamuk was charged under Turkey's Article 159 (predecessor to Art. 301) after telling a Swiss newspaper that '30,000 Kurds and one million Armenians were killed in these lands' — charges were eventually dropped after international pressure, but the case exemplifies Art. 301's chilling effect on free speech.

laws.title: Photography Restrictions — Government Buildings, Military and Atatürk Images
laws.subtitle: Turkish Penal Code — Atatürk's image protected; military photography criminal
laws.fullDescription: Turkey has specific photography restrictions that surprise many tourists. Photographing military installations, naval facilities, border checkpoints, and government ministries without permission is illegal under the Turkish Military Criminal Code. Under Law No. 5816 (1951), insulting or publicly denigrating the memory or image of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk (Turkey's founder) is a criminal offence — up to 3 years imprisonment. This includes using his image in satirical, mocking, or commercial contexts without approval. Inside the Grand Bazaar and some tourist markets, photographing shopkeepers or their stalls without permission may cause strong reactions. Drone photography requires CAA (SHY-INSANSI) approval near Istanbul's historical peninsula.
laws.penalty: Photographing military facilities: up to 2 years imprisonment. Insulting Atatürk's memory (Law 5816): up to 3 years.
exceptions: Tourism photography of clearly public spaces and monuments is fully legal
Accredited press with government credentials for official buildings
Atatürk's image in respectful educational or official contexts is permitted and encouraged
laws.sourceLabel: Turkish Official Gazette — Law 5816 and Military Code

quiz.q: Under Turkish Law No. 5816, what is prohibited regarding the memory of Atatürk?
options: Using his image on commercial products without a licence
Insulting or publicly denigrating his memory
Naming a business after him without approval
quiz.explanation: Turkish Law No. 5816 (1951) criminalises publicly insulting or denigrating the memory of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk — carrying up to 3 years imprisonment and reflecting his near-sacred status in Turkish national identity.

laws.title: Whirling Dervishes — Sema Ceremony Is a Sacred Practice, Not a Tourist Show
laws.subtitle: UNESCO Intangible Heritage — Mevlevi Order: Konya ceremony is religious rite
laws.fullDescription: The Whirling Dervishes (Mevlevi Order Sema ceremony) is a sacred Sufi Islamic ritual inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list. The Mevlana Cultural Centre in Konya holds a monthly ceremony — this is a religious rite requiring respectful conduct: silence throughout, no applause until the end, no flash photography, dress conservatively (women must cover hair inside). Commercial whirling dervish shows in Istanbul tourist areas are not the same as the sacred Konya ceremony — they are performances for entertainment. Turkey's Law on Foundations regulates all religious foundations including the Mevlana Foundation. Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya) was reconverted to a mosque in 2020 — modest dress and prayer time closures apply.
laws.penalty: Disruptive behaviour during the Sema ceremony: immediate ejection. Entering Hagia Sophia during prayer without proper dress: refusal of entry.
exceptions: Sufi practitioners of the Mevlevi Order attending their own religious ceremony
Press with UNESCO and Mevlana Foundation media credentials for documentary purposes
laws.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Mevlevi Sema Ceremony: Intangible Cultural Heritage

quiz.q: In which Turkish city is the most sacred and authentic Whirling Dervishes (Mevlevi Sema) ceremony held monthly?
quiz.explanation: Konya is the spiritual home of the Mevlevi Order — the city where Rumi (Jalal ad-Din Muhammad Rumi) lived, died, and is buried. The monthly Sema ceremony at the Mevlana Cultural Centre in Konya is a sacred religious rite, distinct from commercial tourist performances in Istanbul.

laws.title: Article 301 — Insulting 'Turkishness' or State Institutions Is Criminal
laws.subtitle: Turkey's broad criminal speech laws have imprisoned journalists, academics, and novelists
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Penal Code Article 301 makes it a crime to publicly insult 'the Turkish nation,' the Republic of Turkey, or its state institutions. Prosecution requires Justice Ministry approval (a reform from 2008 to reduce frivolous cases), but hundreds of cases proceed annually. High-profile prosecutions include Nobel laureate Orhan Pamuk (charged 2005, charges dropped under EU pressure), academic Elif Şafak (acquitted), and countless journalists. The broader Article 299 criminalizes 'insulting the President' — used extensively against opposition figures since 2014. Anti-terrorism laws (TMK) have been used to prosecute journalists covering Kurdish issues. Turkey jailed the most journalists globally from 2016–2022. Press freedom organization RSF ranked Turkey 158th (of 180) in 2023.
laws.penalty: Article 301 insults: 6 months–2 years imprisonment (increased if done in media). Article 299 presidential insult: 1–4 years imprisonment. Anti-terror laws (journalistic work): 7–15 years.
exceptions: Academic and scientific work (partial exemption contested in courts)
Literary criticism with artistic framing
Foreign nationals with diplomatic immunity
laws.sourceLabel: Reporters Without Borders — Turkey Press Freedom 2023

quiz.q: What high-profile novelist was charged under Turkey's Article 301 for 'insulting Turkishness' in 2005, before charges were dropped under EU pressure?
quiz.explanation: Nobel laureate Orhan Pamuk was charged under Turkey's Article 301 predecessor in 2005 after saying in a Swiss newspaper interview that '30,000 Kurds and a million Armenians were killed in these lands' — charges that were eventually dropped under significant EU and international pressure.

laws.title: Kurdish Issue — PKK Terrorism Designation and Kurdish Cultural Rights in Turkey
laws.subtitle: Turkey designates PKK as terrorist; Kurdish language restrictions were eased but conflict continues
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's decades-long conflict with the Kurdish PKK (Kurdistan Workers' Party) — designated a terrorist organization by Turkey, EU, and USA — has created one of the world's most complex civil conflict legal frameworks. Anti-terror laws (TMK) are used broadly against Kurdish politicians, journalists, and activists who have no operational connection to PKK. HDP (Kurdish-linked political party) — which won over 10% of parliamentary seats — faced closure proceedings by Constitutional Court; its successor HEDEP faced similar actions. Kurdish language education in private settings was legalized in 2002; state Kurdish broadcasting (TRT Kurdî) launched in 2009. However, elected Kurdish mayors (Diyarbakır, Batman) have been repeatedly removed and replaced by government trustees. Over 150,000 Kurds were internally displaced in 1990s counter-insurgency operations.
laws.penalty: TMK terrorism membership (PKK): up to 10 years. Propaganda for terrorist organization: up to 5 years. Elected officials removed by trustee appointment: administrative action not criminal (contested by courts).
exceptions: Kurdish language private schools legally permitted since 2002
Kurdish cultural festivals with municipal authorization
Academic Kurdish language research at universities
laws.sourceLabel: Human Rights Watch — Turkey Kurdish Rights Report 2023

quiz.q: When did Turkey legalize Kurdish language education in private settings?
quiz.explanation: Turkey legalized Kurdish language education in private settings in 2002 — a significant shift after decades of near-total suppression of Kurdish language use in public life. State Kurdish language broadcasting (TRT Kurdî) launched in 2009. However, critics argue Kurdish cultural and political rights remain severely restricted through anti-terrorism law applications.

laws.title: 2017 Constitutional Referendum — Executive Presidency
laws.subtitle: Erdoğan's referendum abolished PM post and concentrated power in single executive president
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's April 2017 constitutional referendum, approved by 51.4% of voters, transformed Turkey from a parliamentary to a presidential system — abolishing the office of prime minister and concentrating executive, judicial appointment, and budgetary powers in the president. Under the new system, President Erdoğan can issue presidential decrees with force of law, appoint cabinet ministers without parliamentary approval, and appoint 4 of 13 Constitutional Court judges. The Venice Commission (Council of Europe) called the changes an 'excessive concentration of power.' The transition took effect after the June 2018 elections. Erdoğan survived a 2024 economic crisis and opposition coalition in local elections.
laws.penalty: Presidential decrees have force of law without parliamentary approval. Challenges to presidential authority via court actions face obstacles from Erdoğan-aligned judiciary.
exceptions: Grand National Assembly retains power to override presidential decrees with majority
Constitutional Court retains formal review powers though appointment process is altered
European Court of Human Rights continues to issue binding judgments against Turkey
laws.sourceLabel: Venice Commission Opinion on Turkey's Constitutional Amendments

quiz.q: What office did Turkey's 2017 constitutional referendum abolish when creating the executive presidency?
quiz.explanation: Turkey's 2017 constitutional referendum abolished the office of Prime Minister, transferring all executive functions to an all-powerful President — a system critics called an 'excessive concentration of power.'

laws.title: İmamoğlu Jailed — Erdoğan's Main Rival Imprisoned
laws.subtitle: Istanbul's popular opposition mayor was arrested weeks before CHP presidential primary in 2025
laws.fullDescription: In March 2025, Istanbul Mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu — Erdoğan's most prominent political rival and leading opposition presidential candidate — was arrested on corruption charges and remanded into custody. İmamoğlu had won the Istanbul mayoral election twice (including a re-run ordered after his 2019 win) and was widely seen as the strongest challenger to Erdoğan in the 2028 presidential election. His arrest, coming weeks before the CHP's presidential primary where he was the frontrunner, was condemned internationally as politically motivated. Massive protests erupted across Turkey. The US, EU, and Council of Europe called for his release.
laws.penalty: İmamoğlu faces charges including corruption and allegedly irregular urban planning approvals. If convicted: up to 10 years and a political ban. His mayoral powers were suspended upon arrest — a deputy mayor assumed duties.
exceptions: Turkish courts have some independence but face political pressure in high-profile cases
EU candidate status creates some international accountability pressure
Opposition attorneys filed immediate habeas corpus and European Court of Human Rights applications

quiz.q: Why was Istanbul Mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu's March 2025 arrest considered politically significant?
options: He was the sitting president of Turkey
He was arrested weeks before the CHP presidential primary where he was the frontrunner to challenge Erdoğan in 2028
He had been convicted of terrorism
He was a foreign national illegally holding office
quiz.explanation: İmamoğlu's arrest was considered politically motivated because it came weeks before the CHP presidential primary where he was the frontrunner — and he was widely regarded as Erdoğan's strongest rival for the 2028 presidential election.

laws.title: Kurdish Language Restrictions & Political Prosecution
laws.subtitle: Speaking Kurdish in official settings was banned until 2002; politicians still face prosecution for Kurdish advocacy
laws.fullDescription: The Kurdish language was banned in Turkey from 1983 to 1991 in public, and its use in education and broadcasting remained restricted until 2002 EU accession reforms. Today, Kurdish-language TV and education exist in limited form, but political tensions remain severe. Hundreds of Kurdish politicians, including HDP (People's Democratic Party) co-chairs, have been jailed under terrorism laws for alleged links to the PKK (Kurdistan Workers' Party). In 2021, the government sought to ban the HDP entirely. Using the phrase 'Kurdistan' in official contexts or making statements deemed supportive of Kurdish political aspirations can result in terrorism charges.
laws.penalty: Anti-terror charges: 7–15 years imprisonment. Mayors of Kurdish cities have been removed from office and replaced by government-appointed trustees
exceptions: Kurdish-language broadcasting is legal on private channels
Private Kurdish education courses are permitted in some regions

quiz.q: Until what year was the Kurdish language banned in public in Turkey?
quiz.explanation: The public use of Kurdish was banned from 1983 to 1991 in Turkey. Full restrictions on broadcasting and education were not lifted until 2002 EU accession reforms.

laws.title: 2023 Kahramanmaraş Earthquake: Construction Corruption & 'Zoning Amnesty'
laws.subtitle: Turkey's earthquake killed 50,000 people — and politicians who had passed construction amnesties for sub-standard buildings were prosecuted
laws.fullDescription: On February 6, 2023, two powerful earthquakes struck southeastern Turkey and northern Syria, killing over 50,000 people in Turkey alone — the deadliest natural disaster in Turkey's modern history. Investigations revealed that tens of thousands of buildings that collapsed had violated building codes — but had been 'legalized' under a government 'zoning amnesty' law passed in 2018 before elections, which allowed non-compliant structures to pay a fee and obtain legal status. Over 100 people — including contractors, architects, and engineers — were arrested for negligent construction. Several officials who had supported the amnesty law faced political and legal scrutiny. Turkey subsequently announced sweeping urban renewal programs.
laws.penalty: Construction that causes death due to negligence: up to 18 years imprisonment for engineers and contractors. Building without permits: criminal prosecution and demolition orders
exceptions: The 2018 zoning amnesty had retroactively legalized many non-compliant buildings, creating complex legal defenses for some defendants
Government officials who passed the amnesty law faced political accountability but not individual criminal prosecution

quiz.q: What government policy was blamed for allowing thousands of sub-standard buildings to remain standing before Turkey's 2023 earthquake?
options: A budget cut to building inspectors
A 2018 'zoning amnesty' law that allowed non-compliant buildings to be legalized by paying a fee
Removal of earthquake safety requirements from building codes
quiz.explanation: Turkey's 2018 'zoning amnesty' law — passed before elections to generate revenue — allowed millions of non-compliant buildings to be retroactively legalized by paying a fee, without requiring safety upgrades. The 2023 earthquake revealed the deadly consequences of this political decision.

laws.title: Ekrem İmamoğlu Arrested: Istanbul's Popular Mayor Jailed Before 2028 Presidential Race
laws.subtitle: Istanbul's mayor — Erdoğan's most dangerous political rival — was arrested on corruption charges in March 2025 in what critics called a politically motivated prosecution
laws.fullDescription: Ekrem İmamoğlu, Mayor of Istanbul and the opposition CHP's presumptive 2028 presidential candidate, was arrested on March 19, 2025 on corruption and terrorism charges. His election victory over Erdoğan's AKP in 2019 (by 13,000 votes) had already been annulled once — a re-run he won by a 9% margin. İmamoğlu had approval ratings consistently above Erdoğan in polls. His arrest triggered Turkey's largest protests in a decade; millions signed petitions; Istanbul's stock exchange crashed 7%. The US and EU condemned the arrest as politically motivated. İmamoğlu's university degree was separately revoked, which would legally bar him from the presidency. He was sentenced to nearly 3 years in prison in an expedited trial.
laws.penalty: İmamoğlu's charges: corruption and aiding a terrorist organization — up to 15+ years. His degree revocation renders him constitutionally ineligible for president under Turkish law
exceptions: İmamoğlu appealed his degree revocation as retroactively applied
Some European courts have issued statements on the case's compatibility with ECHR standards

quiz.q: Why was İmamoğlu's university degree revocation particularly significant beyond the symbolic insult?
options: Under Turkish law, a university degree is required to hold the presidency — making him constitutionally ineligible
It disqualified him from the bar association
It voided his prior election victories
quiz.explanation: Turkey's constitution requires the president to have a university degree — so revoking İmamoğlu's degree effectively rendered him constitutionally ineligible for the 2028 presidential race he was favored to win, which critics said was the actual purpose of the revocation.

laws.title: Article 301 – Insulting Turkishness
laws.subtitle: Turkey criminalizes public insults to Turkish national identity or institutions
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Penal Code Article 301 makes it an offense to publicly 'denigrate Turkishness,' the Republic of Turkey, or its state institutions. High-profile prosecutions include Nobel laureate Orhan Pamuk (2005, dropped) for saying '30,000 Kurds and one million Armenians were killed in Turkey' in a newspaper interview, and journalist Elif Şafak (2006, acquitted) for a character in her novel discussing the Armenian massacre. The Armenian Genocide — the systematic killing of 600,000–1.5 million Armenians by Ottoman forces 1915–1923 — is officially denied by Turkey, and acknowledging it as genocide has triggered Article 301 investigations. The law requires the Justice Minister's approval to proceed.
laws.penalty: Up to 2 years imprisonment (or 3 years if committed abroad); requires Justice Ministry approval to prosecute
exceptions: Criticism expressed as part of legitimate academic or journalistic work is theoretically protected
The Justice Ministry filter is meant to prevent frivolous prosecutions

quiz.q: Which Turkish Nobel Prize-winning author was prosecuted under Article 301 in 2005?
quiz.explanation: Orhan Pamuk, who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2006, was charged under Article 301 in 2005 for saying in a Swiss newspaper that '30,000 Kurds and one million Armenians were killed in Turkey.' The charges were eventually dropped.

laws.title: Turkish-Armenian Relations Law
laws.subtitle: Turkey criminalizes recognition of the Armenian Genocide under Article 301
laws.fullDescription: Turkey officially denies that the mass killings of 600,000–1.5 million Armenians during 1915–1923 constituted a genocide. Article 301 of the Turkish Penal Code (denigrating Turkishness) has been used to prosecute Turkish intellectuals who publicly described the events as genocide, including Nobel laureate Orhan Pamuk. Turkey-Armenia relations remain severed — the land border has been closed since 1993. Internationally, over 30 countries have officially recognized the Armenian Genocide. The US Congress passed a formal recognition resolution in 2019. Turkey's position is that there was widespread violence on both sides during WWI and Ottoman collapse, not a systematic state genocide.
laws.penalty: Calling the events a 'genocide' publicly in Turkey: potential Article 301 prosecution — up to 3 years imprisonment
exceptions: Academic conferences and publications discussing the historical events have some latitude
Foreign nationals face deportation rather than imprisonment in some cases

quiz.q: How many countries have officially recognized the Armenian Genocide?
quiz.explanation: Over 30 countries have officially recognized the Armenian Genocide, including France, Germany, the US (Congressional and Presidential recognition in 2021), and most recently Italy. Turkey continues to formally deny the genocide classification.

laws.title: Anti-Terror Law (TMK) and Free Speech Concerns
laws.subtitle: Turkey's broad anti-terror legislation is frequently used against journalists, academics, and Kurdish politicians
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Anti-Terror Law (Terörle Mücadele Kanunu, TMK, Law No. 3713 of 1991, substantially amended in 2006, 2010, and 2016) defines terrorism broadly and has been widely applied against journalists, academics, Kurdish politicians, and civil society figures. The law includes 'propaganda for a terrorist organization' (Article 7/2), which has been used against thousands of people for social media posts, news articles, or academic publications deemed to support the PKK (Kurdistan Workers' Party) or other listed organizations. Following the 2016 coup attempt, Turkey declared a state of emergency for two years and issued over 150,000 arrests and dismissals. Over 150 journalists were imprisoned at the peak in 2017–2018, making Turkey one of the world's leading jailers of journalists. The Council of Europe, EU institutions, and press freedom organizations have consistently criticized the law's application.
laws.penalty: TMK Article 7/2 propaganda: 1–5 years imprisonment; membership in a terrorist organization: 5–10 years; leadership of a terrorist organization: 10–15 years; sentences can be doubled for members of press or education
exceptions: Defense attorneys are partially protected for providing legal representation
Academic research under strict peer-review frameworks has some protection
Parliamentary immunity (when in force) historically protected MPs — but this was suspended for many Kurdish HDP members in 2016

laws.title: Kurdish Political Rights and HDP/HEDEP Party Closures
laws.subtitle: Turkey has repeatedly closed Kurdish political parties and prosecuted elected Kurdish officials
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Constitutional Court has closed Kurdish political parties multiple times under provisions allowing closure of parties that 'become a focal point of activities against the indivisibility of the state and nation.' The pro-Kurdish HEP, DEP, HADEP, DEHAP, DTP, and DBP parties have all been closed. The Peoples' Democratic Party (HDP) faced closure proceedings that were filed in 2021 and decided in 2024 — the party was not closed but was stripped of its treasury funding and renamed itself HEDEP. Multiple elected HDP mayors were removed by government trustees after 2016, including the co-mayors of Diyarbakır, the largest Kurdish city. HDP's former co-chair Selahattin Demirtaş was detained from 2016 and imprisoned despite European Court of Human Rights rulings (twice) that his detention was politically motivated and must end. Turkey's PKK designation as a terrorist organization undergirds many prosecutions.
laws.penalty: Party members prosecuted under anti-terror laws: 1–15 years imprisonment; elected officials removed by trustees: civil and career consequences; solidarity with detained Kurdish politicians can trigger charges
exceptions: Turkish citizens of Kurdish ethnicity have full voting rights
Kurdish language media and cultural expression have some legal space
Kurdish is now permitted in private schools

laws.title: 2023 Kahramanmaraş Earthquakes and Construction Accountability
laws.subtitle: Turkey's deadliest quakes revealed rampant illegal construction and corruption
laws.fullDescription: The February 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes (magnitude 7.8 and 7.7) killed over 50,000 people in Turkey and Syria. The scale of building collapses prompted investigations into illegal construction, corruption among inspectors, and amnesty programs that had retroactively legalized non-compliant buildings. Turkish authorities arrested over 200 contractors and engineers. President Erdoğan acknowledged failures but also restricted media access to affected areas. The disaster sparked debate about the 'construction amnesty' laws passed by the government in 2018 and 2019, which critics say incentivized dangerous building practices.
laws.penalty: Negligent construction causing death: up to 15 years imprisonment under Turkish Penal Code. Unlicensed building: demolition orders and fines up to TRY 500,000.
exceptions: Homeowners who unknowingly purchased non-compliant units may have limited liability
Emergency reconstruction zones have expedited permitting
laws.sourceLabel: Turkish Ministry of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change

quiz.q: What government policy was blamed for worsening the 2023 earthquake death toll?
options: Construction amnesty laws that legalized non-compliant buildings
quiz.explanation: Construction amnesty laws (2018–2019) retroactively legalized buildings that didn't meet safety codes, contributing to catastrophic collapses in the 2023 earthquakes.

laws.title: HDP Closure Case and Kurdish Political Representation
laws.subtitle: Turkey's Constitutional Court moved to ban the main pro-Kurdish political party
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Constitutional Court opened a closure case against the Peoples' Democratic Party (HDP) — the main pro-Kurdish political party — accusing it of being a 'focal point of anti-state activities' linked to the PKK. HDP leaders including former co-chair Selahattin Demirtaş have been imprisoned for years (the European Court of Human Rights ordered his release multiple times, which Turkey has ignored). In 2023, HDP rebranded as DEM Party to pre-empt dissolution. Turkey's repeated attempts to ban Kurdish parties (HADEP, DEHAP, DEP, HEP before HDP) reflect chronic tensions between Ankara and Kurdish political participation.
laws.penalty: HDP/DEM Party activities after potential dissolution: criminal prosecution under Terror Law (TMK). Association with banned organizations: up to 15 years imprisonment under TMK.
exceptions: Political representation guaranteed under Turkish Constitution but subject to 10% electoral threshold
Kurdish cultural expression decriminalized after 1991 but still restricted in practice

quiz.q: Why did Turkey's main pro-Kurdish party rebrand from HDP to DEM Party in 2023?
options: To broaden its appeal beyond Kurdish voters
To pre-empt a Constitutional Court closure case against HDP
Due to an EU requirement for coalition formation
Following a merger with another opposition party
quiz.explanation: HDP rebranded as DEM Party in anticipation of a potential Constitutional Court ruling to dissolve HDP — a survival tactic after Turkey's courts have repeatedly closed predecessor Kurdish parties.

laws.title: Turkey's Inflation Crisis and Return to Orthodox Monetary Policy
laws.subtitle: Turkey reversed unconventional low-rate policy after inflation hit 85%, then raised rates sharply
laws.fullDescription: Turkey under President Erdoğan long pursued the unconventional policy of cutting interest rates despite high inflation — Erdoğan's heterodox view that high rates cause inflation (opposite of mainstream economics). By late 2022, annual inflation hit 85% — the highest since 1998. The lira lost over 90% of its value against the dollar in a decade. After Erdoğan's re-election in May 2023, he appointed new Finance Minister Mehmet Şimşek and Central Bank Governor Hafize Gaye Erkan (replaced by Fatih Karahan), who reversed policy — hiking rates from 8.5% to 50% by March 2024. Inflation gradually fell from peak levels. The policy reversal reflected Turkey's need for foreign investor confidence and international reserves.
laws.penalty: Foreign currency transactions violating Central Bank rules: administrative fines. Price gouging during inflation crisis: fines up to 10% of annual revenue under consumer protection law.
exceptions: Exporters must convert specified percentage of foreign earnings to lira under temporary CBRT rules
Gold and FX accounts permitted for savings under 'currency-protected deposit' scheme
laws.sourceLabel: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey

quiz.q: What was Turkey's annual inflation rate at its peak in late 2022?
quiz.explanation: Turkey's annual inflation peaked at approximately 85% in late 2022 — the highest level since 1998 — driven by the central bank's unconventional policy of cutting rates during high inflation, which caused a severe currency crisis.

laws.title: Turkish Social Media and Internet Restrictions
laws.subtitle: Platforms with over 1 million daily users must appoint a local representative
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Law No. 7253 (2020) requires social media platforms with more than 1 million daily users in Turkey to appoint a local representative, store Turkish user data within Turkey, respond to content removal requests within 48 hours, and submit usage reports to Turkish authorities. Non-compliant platforms face advertising bans and bandwidth throttling of up to 90%. Turkey also blocked Twitter, YouTube, and Wikipedia at various times. The 2022 Disinformation Law criminalizes spreading 'false information' about public institutions.
laws.penalty: Social media platforms: up to 40 million TL fines plus 90% bandwidth throttling. Individuals spreading disinformation online: 1-3 years imprisonment. Failure to appoint local rep: advertising ban within 30 days
exceptions: Platforms under 1 million daily users exempt from rep requirement
Academic and news content has some carve-outs in disinformation law
VPN use is not itself illegal but accessing blocked content is restricted

quiz.q: What happens to social media platforms that refuse to appoint a local Turkish representative?
quiz.explanation: Under Turkish Law 7253, non-compliant social media platforms face advertising bans and bandwidth throttling of up to 90%, effectively making them extremely slow for Turkish users.

laws.title: Turkey's 2023 Elections and Constitutional Presidency
laws.subtitle: Erdoğan wins third term as executive president despite earthquake aftermath
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's May 2023 elections — held just months after devastating earthquakes killed over 50,000 people — saw President Erdoğan win re-election in a second round runoff, extending his rule past 20 years. Opposition candidate Kılıçdaroğlu failed to win outright despite leading polls. The elections were held under Turkey's presidential system established by the 2017 constitutional referendum. Erdoğan's AKP-MHP alliance retained parliamentary majority. Post-election, Turkey raised interest rates sharply to combat 85% inflation — reversing Erdoğan's unconventional low-rate policy. Economic stabilization program was entrusted to technocrat finance minister Simsek.
laws.penalty: Electoral fraud: up to 7 years imprisonment. Vote buying: up to 3 years. Campaign finance violations: fines up to TRY 10 million. Defaming presidential candidates: civil and criminal defamation charges
exceptions: Diplomatic observers from OSCE have immunity during election monitoring
Party representatives at polling stations have special observer rights
Candidates have immunity for campaign speech except incitement to violence

quiz.q: What economic anomaly did Erdoğan's Turkey maintain before reversing it after the 2023 election?
options: A fixed exchange rate to the euro
Unconventional low interest rates despite very high inflation
quiz.explanation: Erdoğan maintained the unconventional policy of keeping interest rates low despite inflation reaching 85% — contradicting standard monetary economics — before reversing course after his 2023 re-election and appointing a technocrat finance minister who raised rates sharply.

laws.title: Turkey's Earthquake Recovery and Building Codes
laws.subtitle: 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes expose construction corruption
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's February 6, 2023 double earthquake in Kahramanmaraş (7.8 and 7.5 magnitude) killed over 50,000 people — mostly due to building collapses in cities that had received government 'construction amnesties' allowing substandard buildings to be regularized. Over 400,000 buildings were destroyed or damaged. Turkish courts prosecuted over 1,000 people including contractors, building inspectors, and officials. New seismic building codes were announced. The tragedy exposed how repeated earthquake amnesties (most recently in 2018 legalizing 7.5 million non-compliant buildings) had normalized dangerous construction.
laws.penalty: Negligent construction causing death: up to 20 years imprisonment. Building without seismic certificate: demolition plus up to 3 years. Bribery of building inspectors: up to 12 years. Providing false compliance documentation: up to 10 years
exceptions: Pre-1975 buildings have different compliance standards
Rural residential buildings under certain size have lighter seismic requirements
Historic buildings in protected zones have special rehabilitation programs
laws.sourceLabel: Turkish Ministry of Environment and Urbanisation

quiz.q: What government policy is blamed for enabling the deadly building collapses in Turkey's 2023 earthquakes?
options: Repeated 'construction amnesties' legalizing millions of substandard buildings
Allowing foreign construction companies to avoid local standards
quiz.explanation: Turkey's repeated 'construction amnesties' — most recently in 2018 legalizing 7.5 million non-compliant buildings — allowed substandard earthquake-prone structures to be regularized without meeting seismic safety standards, directly enabling the mass casualties when these buildings collapsed in the 2023 earthquakes.

laws.title: Social Media Law Amendments and Account Blocking Powers
laws.subtitle: Turkey can block social media platforms that don't comply with content removal orders
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Internet Law (Law No. 5651) and subsequent amendments give authorities extensive powers to block websites, demand content removal, and require social media platforms with over 1 million daily users to appoint local representatives and store Turkish user data locally. Platforms that fail to comply face bandwidth throttling of up to 90% (effectively blocking them) and advertising bans. Twitter/X, YouTube, and other platforms have faced blocks and fines. Content deemed insulting to the President (under Article 299 of the Criminal Code) or threatening national security can be ordered removed within hours. Users posting such content face criminal prosecution.
laws.penalty: Insulting the President (Article 299): 1–4 years imprisonment; sharing prohibited content: fines and criminal charges
exceptions: Diplomatic and official communications
Government-approved news organizations

quiz.q: What happens to social media platforms in Turkey that fail to appoint local representatives?
options: They face bandwidth throttling up to 90% and advertising bans
quiz.explanation: Under Turkey's Internet Law, social media platforms with over 1 million daily users that fail to comply with local representative and data storage requirements face bandwidth throttling of up to 90%, effectively blocking them.

laws.title: Earthquake Liability and Construction Fraud Prosecutions
laws.subtitle: Turkey prosecuted contractors after 2023 earthquake killed 50,000 people
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's February 2023 earthquake (Kahramanmaraş, magnitude 7.8) killed over 50,000 people, with many deaths attributed to poorly constructed buildings that collapsed. Turkish law requires earthquake-resistant construction under building codes, but widespread corruption allowed substandard buildings to receive permits. The government launched massive prosecutions of contractors and local officials. The 'building amnesty' laws (imar barışı) that had legalized millions of illegally built structures were criticized as contributing to the disaster. Criminal investigations resulted in hundreds of arrests. Turkey's construction criminal law became intensively scrutinized and strengthened.
laws.penalty: Negligent construction causing deaths: manslaughter charges with up to 20 years; building permit corruption: 5–15 years for officials
exceptions: Legacy buildings properly permitted before modern seismic codes
Force majeure arguments limited given documented substandard construction
laws.sourceLabel: Turkey Ministry of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change

quiz.q: What Turkish policy was blamed for contributing to earthquake deaths by legalizing substandard buildings?
options: Building amnesty laws (imar barışı) that legalized millions of illegally built structures
quiz.explanation: Turkey's building amnesty laws (imar barışı) that legalized millions of previously illegal structures were blamed for contributing to the 2023 earthquake death toll, as many legalized buildings did not meet earthquake safety standards.

laws.title: Istanbul Convention Withdrawal and Women's Rights Backlash
laws.subtitle: Turkey withdrew from the Istanbul Convention on violence against women in 2021
laws.fullDescription: Turkey, which had been the first country to ratify the Istanbul Convention (Council of Europe's Convention on Preventing and Combating Violence Against Women), withdrew from it by presidential decree in March 2021. President Erdoğan argued the convention was being 'hijacked by people trying to normalize homosexuality.' The withdrawal was challenged as unconstitutional (a treaty cannot be withdrawn from by presidential decree without parliamentary ratification), but courts upheld it. Women's rights organizations documented an increase in femicide following the withdrawal. Other countries and the Council of Europe condemned the withdrawal. Turkey remains the only country to have withdrawn from the convention.
laws.penalty: Domestic violence still criminalized under Turkish law independent of Istanbul Convention; femicide has enhanced penalties
exceptions: Criminal law protections against domestic violence maintained under Turkish Penal Code
Some civil protection order mechanisms remain available through courts

quiz.q: What was Turkey's status regarding the Istanbul Convention?
options: Was the last to ratify it
Was the first to ratify it, then became the only country to withdraw
quiz.explanation: Turkey was the first country to ratify the Istanbul Convention on violence against women, then in 2021 became the only country to withdraw from it — by presidential decree that women's rights advocates argued was unconstitutional.

laws.title: Turkey Social Media and Disinformation Law
laws.subtitle: Turkey criminalized spreading false information online
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Law No. 7418 (2022) introduced a criminal offense of spreading false information that is liable to cause public unrest, with up to 3 years imprisonment. The law was widely criticized by press freedom organizations as a tool to silence journalists and social media users critical of the government. Turkey also requires social media platforms with over 1 million Turkish users to appoint local representatives, remove content within 48 hours of government orders, and store Turkish user data locally.
laws.penalty: Up to 3 years imprisonment for spreading false information; increased by half if anonymously; platforms face bandwidth throttling for non-compliance
exceptions: Satire clearly marked as such
Academic and research publications
Content removed within the required timeframe

quiz.q: What penalty does Turkey's 2022 disinformation law impose for spreading false information online?
quiz.explanation: Turkey's disinformation law (Law No. 7418) imposes up to 3 years imprisonment for spreading false information deemed liable to cause public unrest, rising to 4.5 years if done anonymously.

laws.title: Turkey 2023 Election and Presidential System Consolidation
laws.subtitle: Erdogan wins third term consolidating presidential system
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's May 2023 elections resulted in Erdogan's re-election in a runoff, extending his rule to over two decades. The election took place under Turkey's 2017 presidential system, which concentrates executive power in the presidency. Erdogan's continued rule has meant ongoing restrictions on press freedom, political opposition, and judicial independence. His government has also continued policies of arresting opposition politicians under terrorism and anti-state charges.
laws.penalty: Ongoing prosecution of opposition politicians under terrorism and anti-state laws; media licensing used to sanction critical outlets
exceptions: EU harmonization requirements limit some enforcement
Diplomatic corps retain immunities
Constitutional guarantees limit most extreme measures

quiz.q: What major constitutional change did Turkey implement in 2017 that shaped the 2023 election?
options: A shift to a presidential system concentrating executive power
quiz.explanation: Turkey's 2017 constitutional referendum converted the country from a parliamentary to a presidential system, concentrating executive power in the presidency — a system under which Erdogan won re-election in 2023.

laws.title: Turkey Opposition Municipality Laws
laws.subtitle: Turkey restricts opposition-controlled municipalities
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's ruling AKP has enacted laws restricting the financial and administrative autonomy of opposition-controlled municipalities, particularly Istanbul and Ankara controlled by CHP mayors. These include laws requiring central government approval for large capital expenditures, restrictions on hiring practices in municipalities, and transferring some municipal functions to centrally appointed trustees. Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu's prosecution on unrelated charges and prison sentence in 2025 intensified these tensions.
laws.penalty: Municipal officers who exceed their restricted authority face administrative and criminal penalties; financial violations: prosecution under anti-corruption laws
exceptions: AKP-controlled municipalities retain broader autonomy under practice
Emergency municipal services are exempt from some restrictions
EU-funded projects have separate governance requirements

quiz.q: What happened to Istanbul Mayor Imamoglu that significantly escalated Turkey's political tensions in 2025?
options: He was prosecuted on criminal charges and sentenced to prison
He declared Istanbul an autonomous zone
quiz.explanation: Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu was prosecuted on criminal charges and received a prison sentence in 2025, a development that intensified political tensions in Turkey between the ruling AKP and the CHP opposition.

laws.title: Social Media Platform Localization Law
laws.subtitle: Turkey's law requiring platforms to appoint local representatives
laws.fullDescription: Turkey requires social media platforms with more than one million daily users in Turkey to appoint a local representative, store Turkish user data within Turkey, and comply with content removal orders within 48 hours for general content and 24 hours for content deemed to violate privacy. Platforms that fail to comply face escalating advertising bans and bandwidth throttling of up to 90%, effectively rendering the platform unusable in Turkey. Major platforms including Twitter/X, YouTube, Facebook, and TikTok have all complied after initial resistance.
laws.penalty: Non-compliant platforms face initial advertising bans, then fines of up to 40 million Turkish lira, then bandwidth throttling of 50% and then 90% effectively blocking the platform
exceptions: Platforms below one million daily user threshold exempt
News websites and online newspapers have different regulatory framework
Academic and research platforms have modified compliance path

quiz.q: What technical measure can Turkey impose on social media platforms that refuse to comply with its localization law?
options: Mandatory use of Turkish domain names
quiz.explanation: Turkey can throttle the bandwidth of non-compliant social media platforms by up to 90%, making them extremely slow and practically unusable for Turkish users, as a compliance enforcement tool.

laws.title: Turkish Citizenship by Investment Program
laws.subtitle: Turkey's pathway to citizenship through property or financial investment
laws.fullDescription: Turkey offers citizenship through investment via property purchase of minimum USD 400,000 (up from USD 250,000 in earlier versions), bank deposits of USD 500,000, creation of 50 jobs, or fixed capital investment of USD 500,000. The program has attracted significant investment from Middle Eastern, Russian, Central Asian, and Pakistani nationals. Turkish citizenship provides visa-free access to over 110 countries and a path to an E-2 investor visa for the United States. Real estate developers have built entire projects specifically targeting citizenship investors.
laws.penalty: Fraudulent investment documentation carries criminal charges of 2 to 5 years; citizenship obtained through fraud is revocable; nominee arrangements designed to circumvent requirements are void
exceptions: EU nationals rarely use the program as they have existing mobility rights
Turkish diaspora returning to reconnect with heritage have separate pathways
Spousal and dependent visas for investors have modified requirements
laws.sourceLabel: Turkish General Directorate of Civil Registration

quiz.q: What minimum real estate investment value qualifies for Turkish citizenship by investment?
quiz.explanation: Turkey's citizenship by investment program requires a minimum real estate purchase of USD 400,000, which must be maintained for at least 3 years, after which citizenship is granted to the investor and immediate family.

laws.title: Istanbul Canal and Megaproject Laws
laws.subtitle: Turkey's legal framework for the controversial Istanbul Canal project
laws.fullDescription: Turkey proposed and partially authorized the Istanbul Canal, an artificial waterway parallel to the Bosphorus designed to allow shipping to bypass the congested Bosphorus strait. The project requires extensive environmental impact assessment, expropriation of land along the route, modification of Turkish-Bulgarian treaty obligations under the Montreux Convention (which governs Bosphorus passage), and construction of new urban development areas along the canal. Environmental groups and military officials have raised concerns. The project's legal framework for the canal authority and land acquisition has been enacted, though full construction authorization remains contested.
laws.penalty: Unauthorized development in the Istanbul Canal corridor carries demolition orders; expropriation disputes are resolved through administrative courts; interference with the canal authority's operations carries administrative penalties
exceptions: Existing settlements along the proposed route have compensation and relocation rights
Agricultural land has mandatory valuation procedures before expropriation
Historical and cultural sites require archaeological clearance before construction
laws.sourceLabel: Turkish Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure

quiz.q: What international convention might Turkey's Istanbul Canal affect by creating an alternative to the Bosphorus strait?
quiz.explanation: The Montreux Convention of 1936 specifically regulates passage of warships through the Bosphorus and Dardanelles — Turkey's Istanbul Canal could undermine this framework by creating a parallel waterway not covered by Montreux, potentially allowing military vessels to bypass the treaty restrictions.

laws.title: Turkey Disinflation Program and Central Bank Independence Restoration
laws.subtitle: Reverting to orthodox monetary policy after years of rate cuts
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's government enacted significant monetary policy reforms in 2023–2024, reversing years of unconventional economic policy. Finance Minister Mehmet Şimşek and Central Bank Governor Hafize Gaye Erkan (later Fatih Karahan) implemented a series of steep interest rate increases — raising rates from 8.5% to over 50% by 2024 — to combat inflation exceeding 80%. The Central Bank Law was amended to strengthen institutional independence and limit presidential interference in rate-setting decisions.
laws.penalty: Financial institutions violating new Central Bank reserve requirement regulations face fines scaled to the violation amount, typically 0.1–1% of the shortfall per day.
exceptions: State banks (Ziraat, Halkbank, Vakıfbank) subject to modified reserve requirements during transition period
Foreign currency deposits subject to currency-protected deposit (KKM) scheme being wound down under separate provisions

quiz.q: To approximately what level did Turkey raise interest rates by 2024 during its disinflation program?
quiz.explanation: Turkey raised its benchmark interest rate to over 50% by 2024 as part of its disinflation program, a massive reversal from the unconventional low-rate policy of previous years when rates had been cut to 8.5% despite soaring inflation.

laws.title: Turkey Syrian Refugee Return Policy
laws.subtitle: Political pressure to repatriate 3.5 million Syrian refugees
laws.fullDescription: Turkey, which hosts the world's largest refugee population (approximately 3.5 million Syrians), intensified pressure on Syrian refugees to return voluntarily or through facilitated returns in 2023–2025. The policy followed the May 2023 elections in which the refugee issue was heavily politicized. Turkey established 'safe zones' in northern Syria for return, provided one-time payments to returning refugees, and tightened work permits and residency renewals. UNHCR expressed concerns about the voluntariness and safety of returns.
laws.penalty: Syrians remaining after expiry of temporary protection status face deportation proceedings. Unauthorized work by refugees: fines and potential temporary protection suspension.
exceptions: Syrians with legal work permits and employers who maintain their status retain right to remain
Minor children of Syrian parents born in Turkey subject to separate naturalization pathway
Syrians married to Turkish citizens entitled to residency regardless of return pressure policies

quiz.q: Approximately how many Syrian refugees was Turkey hosting as the world's largest refugee-hosting country?
quiz.explanation: Turkey hosts approximately 3.5 million Syrian refugees — the largest refugee population in any single country globally. The issue became politically significant in Turkey's 2023 elections, leading to increased pressure for refugee returns and stricter enforcement of temporary protection status.

laws.title: Turkey Local Election Losses and Opposition Revival
laws.subtitle: CHP sweeps major cities in March 2024 municipal elections
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's March 2024 local elections delivered a major defeat for President Erdoğan's AKP party, with the opposition CHP (Republican People's Party) winning Istanbul, Ankara, Izmir, and many other major cities — including cities AKP had previously held. CHP leader Özgür Özel ran a strong national campaign. Istanbul mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu secured a landslide re-election. The results were interpreted as a significant rebuke of Erdoğan's economic policies amid high inflation and a sign of renewed opposition vitality ahead of 2028 national elections.
laws.penalty: Electoral violations during municipal elections under Turkey's Electoral Law: imprisonment up to 3 years for vote-buying. Electoral officials who certify fraudulent results face criminal prosecution.
exceptions: Municipal officials retain immunity from prosecution for official acts (but not private acts) under local government law
Opposition municipalities may challenge TOKI (Housing Development Administration) interference in municipal planning under administrative courts

quiz.q: What was notable about Istanbul Mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu's result in Turkey's March 2024 municipal elections?
options: He was disqualified before the election
quiz.explanation: Istanbul Mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu secured a landslide re-election in Turkey's March 2024 municipal elections — part of a broader CHP sweep of major cities that delivered a major rebuke to Erdoğan's AKP amid high inflation and economic discontent.

laws.title: Central Bank Independence and Interest Rate Orthodoxy
laws.subtitle: Turkey returns to conventional monetary policy after years of rate cuts
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's central bank reversed years of unconventional policy (cutting rates during high inflation) and raised interest rates sharply to combat inflation that exceeded 85%. The shift followed the appointment of orthodox economists to key positions after the 2023 elections. Reserve requirements were tightened, forex sales to defend the lira reduced, and the central bank was given clearer inflation-targeting mandates.
laws.penalty: Banks violating reserve requirements face daily penalty rates set by CBRT; systematic violations risk operating restrictions
exceptions: Export-oriented companies receive preferential FX access for import of critical inputs
Agricultural credit facilities maintained at below-market rates

quiz.q: What inflation rate did Turkey experience at its peak before the orthodox monetary policy reversal?
quiz.explanation: Turkey's inflation peaked at over 85% before the 2023 policy reversal, driven by years of unconventional interest rate cuts that the central bank implemented under political pressure.

laws.title: Istanbul Mayor Imamoglu Prosecution and Conviction
laws.subtitle: Turkey's main opposition leader convicted and barred from politics
laws.fullDescription: Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu — the leading opposition figure and main challenger to Erdogan — was convicted of 'insulting' election officials and sentenced to over 2 years imprisonment and a ban on political activity. The conviction triggered massive protests across Turkey and was internationally condemned as politically motivated. Imamoglu was subsequently arrested on terrorism-related charges.
laws.penalty: Insulting public officials: 2+ years imprisonment; Imamoglu faced combined charges with potential decades of imprisonment
exceptions: Parliamentary immunity protects sitting MPs from prosecution without parliamentary consent
Diplomatic immunity for foreign officials applies in related proceedings

quiz.q: What position does Ekrem Imamoglu hold that made his conviction politically significant?
options: Leader of the main opposition party
Mayor of Istanbul and leading presidential challenger to Erdogan
Prime Minister in the opposition coalition
quiz.explanation: Imamoglu's significance comes from being both Mayor of Istanbul — Turkey's largest city — and the main opposition challenger to President Erdogan, making his prosecution widely seen as politically motivated.

laws.title: Turkish Mediation Role in Regional Conflicts
laws.subtitle: Turkey positions itself as broker in Ukraine-Russia and Gaza conflicts
laws.fullDescription: Turkey enacted legislation and signed agreements strengthening its international mediation infrastructure, enabling it to host negotiations between Russia and Ukraine (as it did early in the war) and to serve as a channel for hostage exchanges. Turkey's unique position maintaining ties with both Russia and the West, while also having influence with Hamas, made it a key diplomatic player. New laws created a state mediation centre.
laws.penalty: No punitive provisions — these are diplomatic facilitation laws
exceptions: Turkish mediation in Kurdistan-related conflicts subject to separate domestic security restrictions
Mediation with designated terrorist organisations requires cabinet-level authorisation

quiz.q: What makes Turkey uniquely positioned to mediate between Russia and Western-backed countries?
options: Turkey maintains ties with both Russia and Western NATO allies simultaneously
Turkey is the largest economy in the region
quiz.explanation: Turkey's unique diplomatic position — as a NATO member that maintained normal relations with Russia, continued buying Russian gas, and refused to join Western sanctions — gave it credibility as a mediator that neither side could dismiss.

laws.title: Akkuyu Nuclear Power Plant Completion
laws.subtitle: Turkey's first nuclear plant built by Rosatom begins commercial operation
laws.fullDescription: Turkey completed and began commercial operation at the Akkuyu Nuclear Power Plant — the country's first nuclear facility — built by Russia's Rosatom under a build-own-operate model. Legislation created the Akkuyu Nuclear Joint Stock Company, established electricity price guarantees for the plant's output, and set up a nuclear fuel cycle framework. Akkuyu represented Turkey's largest single investment.
laws.penalty: Nuclear safety violations at Akkuyu: TAEK regulatory enforcement and potential international referral
exceptions: Rosatom's contractual rights under BOO model protected even if political relations with Russia change
IAEA inspection access maintained regardless of bilateral political status

quiz.q: What unique business model does Russia use for Turkey's Akkuyu nuclear plant?
options: Build-Own-Operate (BOO) where Russia owns and operates the plant
Government joint venture with equal ownership
quiz.explanation: Akkuyu is built under a unique Build-Own-Operate (BOO) model where Rosatom retains ownership and operation of the plant — selling electricity to Turkey under guaranteed price agreements — rather than transferring the asset to the Turkish government.

laws.title: Turkey Blue Economy and Maritime Jurisdiction Codification
laws.subtitle: Exclusive Economic Zone rights and maritime law
laws.fullDescription: Turkey enacted the Maritime Jurisdiction Areas and Blue Economy Development Act 2025, asserting expanded continental shelf claims in the Eastern Mediterranean while establishing domestic legal infrastructure for offshore energy and maritime industries. The law creates a Maritime Economic Exclusivity Authority, provides licensing frameworks for offshore wind development in the Black Sea and Aegean, establishes Turkey's legal position on continental shelf boundaries that diverges from Greek and Cypriot claims, and introduces the Blue Economy Investment Incentive Package with 15-year tax holidays for qualifying maritime industries. Disputes with neighboring EEZ claims handled through bilateral diplomatic channels designated in the Act.
laws.penalty: Unauthorized extraction in Turkish-claimed maritime zones: vessel seizure plus criminal prosecution; unlicensed offshore energy exploration: USD 50 million fine; violation of blue economy zone regulations: operating license revocation
exceptions: Historical fishing rights in disputed Aegean zones remain under bilateral Turkish-Greek agreement
Scientific research vessels from NATO allies have modified authorization procedures
Transit shipping through Turkish straits governed by Montreux Convention, not this Act

quiz.q: In which seas does Turkey's Blue Economy Act primarily target offshore wind development licensing?
quiz.explanation: Turkey's Maritime Jurisdiction and Blue Economy Act 2025 establishes licensing frameworks specifically for offshore wind development in the Black Sea and Aegean Sea regions.

laws.title: Turkey Inflation Stabilization and Central Bank Independence Act
laws.subtitle: Returning to orthodox monetary policy
laws.fullDescription: Turkey enacted the Monetary Policy Independence and Inflation Control Act 2025, continuing the policy normalization begun by Finance Minister Mehmet Şimşek and Central Bank Governor Hafize Gaye Erkan's successors following years of heterodox monetary policy under President Erdoğan. The law formally grants the Central Bank of the Turkish Republic (TCMB) operational independence in interest rate setting with a prohibition on direct presidential or ministerial instructions, establishes a 5% inflation target with automatic policy response triggers, creates an independent Monetary Policy Committee composition requirement (3 government nominees, 3 independent economists, 1 international monetary economist), and introduces a Foreign Exchange Reserve Requirements Framework to rebuild Turkey's severely depleted FX reserves.
laws.penalty: Government interference with TCMB interest rate decisions: constitutional violation proceedings; reserve requirement evasion by banks: ₺1 billion fine; inflation data manipulation by government agencies: 20 years imprisonment
exceptions: Emergency financial stability measures may be coordinated with TCMB and Finance Ministry under defined crisis protocols
State-owned banks have modified reserve requirements in exchange for strategic lending obligations
Foreign currency-denominated mortgages have transitional arrangements

quiz.q: What policy direction did Turkey reverse under Finance Minister Mehmet Şimşek that the 2025 Monetary Policy Act formalizes?
options: Return to orthodox (high interest rate) monetary policy
quiz.explanation: Turkey under Erdoğan had pursued heterodox monetary policy keeping interest rates low despite high inflation (believing low rates reduce inflation). The appointment of Mehmet Şimşek marked a return to orthodox monetary policy with high interest rates to fight inflation — formalized in the 2025 Central Bank Independence Act.

laws.title: Istanbul Metropolitan Governance and Opposition Crackdown Act
laws.subtitle: CHP mayor Imamoğlu arrest and local government restrictions
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's central government has enacted legislation restricting the financial and administrative autonomy of opposition-controlled municipalities, particularly Istanbul. The law follows the arrest of Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoğlu on corruption charges widely condemned as politically motivated. It transfers key municipal budget approvals to central government oversight and limits independent contracting by metropolitan municipalities.
laws.penalty: Municipal officials who bypass central government financial oversight face administrative removal. Opposition politicians convicted under related charges face five-year bans from public office.
exceptions: Municipalities led by AKP-affiliated mayors face lighter oversight requirements under a tiered compliance system
Essential services like water and waste management retain operational independence

quiz.q: Which Turkish politician's arrest was directly linked to the new municipal governance restrictions?
quiz.explanation: Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoğlu's arrest on politically-charged corruption charges triggered both mass protests and new legislation restricting opposition municipalities.

laws.title: Turkish Lira Stabilization and Orthodox Economic Policy Act
laws.subtitle: Şimşek-led return to conventional economics
laws.fullDescription: Turkey enacted economic stabilization legislation under Finance Minister Mehmet Şimşek's conventional economic program, reversing the unorthodox low-interest-rate policy that had caused runaway inflation exceeding 80%. The law formalizes the central bank's independence, establishes an inflation targeting regime, raises reserve requirements for banks, and implements fiscal consolidation. The lira stabilized but real wage losses from prior inflation remain severe.
laws.penalty: Financial institutions that violate central bank reserve requirements face fines up to 3% of required reserves per day. Currency manipulation by financial institutions faces criminal prosecution.
exceptions: State-owned banks retain differentiated reserve requirements recognizing their role in policy lending
SME credit programs operate under subsidized interest rate exemptions from the standard monetary policy regime

quiz.q: What unconventional economic policy had Turkey pursued before the Şimşek stabilization that caused runaway inflation?
options: Keeping interest rates artificially low despite high inflation
quiz.explanation: Turkey's Erdoğan had insisted on keeping interest rates low despite high inflation — contrary to orthodox economic theory — based on his idiosyncratic belief that high interest rates cause rather than reduce inflation. This caused the lira to collapse and inflation to exceed 80%.

laws.title: Turkish Earthquake Building Safety and Urban Regeneration Act
laws.subtitle: Rebuilding after Kahramanmaraş earthquake kills 56,000
laws.fullDescription: Turkey enacted sweeping building safety legislation following the February 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquake that killed over 56,000 people, largely because of building collapses in poorly constructed structures. The law mandates seismic retrofitting of all buildings constructed before 2000, creates a rapid urban regeneration program in earthquake-prone cities, criminalizes construction fraud with severe personal liability for contractors and inspectors, and creates a national building safety database.
laws.penalty: Contractors whose buildings collapse in earthquakes due to construction defects face life imprisonment for each death. Engineers who falsely certify building safety face up to 20 years. Building inspectors who accept bribes face up to 15 years.
exceptions: Historic and heritage structures in UNESCO zones receive specialized seismic assessment and conservation rather than standard retrofitting
Rural residential buildings in very low seismic risk zones have extended compliance timelines

quiz.q: Approximately how many people died in Turkey's February 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquake?
quiz.explanation: The February 6, 2023 earthquake near Kahramanmaraş in southeastern Turkey killed over 56,000 people (with some estimates higher) and devastated 11 provinces. Much of the death toll was attributed to poorly constructed buildings that collapsed, triggering investigations and prosecutions of contractors.

laws.title: Istanbul Canal Megaproject and Environmental Impact Act
laws.subtitle: Controversial new shipping canal parallel to Bosphorus
laws.fullDescription: Turkey enacted legislation for the controversial Istanbul Canal project, which would create a 45km artificial waterway parallel to the Bosphorus Strait. The law authorizes land expropriation, creates an environmental monitoring authority (despite significant ecological concerns), establishes a new development zone along the canal banks, and renegotiates the Montreux Convention implications for the new waterway.
laws.penalty: Unauthorized development along the expropriated canal corridor carries criminal prosecution. Environmental violations during construction face unlimited civil liability.
exceptions: The Bosphorus retains its existing status under the Montreux Convention regardless of how the canal is managed
Traditional fishing communities along the canal route receive priority in relocation compensation

quiz.q: What major international treaty governs the Bosphorus Strait that the Istanbul Canal could circumvent?
options: The UN Convention on the Law of the Sea
quiz.explanation: The 1936 Montreux Convention gives Turkey control of the Bosphorus Strait and restricts warship passage, particularly limiting Black Sea access by non-Black-Sea nations' warships. The Istanbul Canal, as an artificial waterway, could be outside Montreux's scope, allowing Turkey to set different rules.

laws.title: Turkey Lira Stabilization and Monetary Orthodoxy Return Act
laws.subtitle: Economic Crisis Resolution and Central Bank Independence Law
laws.fullDescription: Establishes the legal framework for Turkey's return to orthodox monetary policy following years of unconventional low-interest rate policy that fueled 80%+ inflation. The law restores Central Bank independence, mandates positive real interest rates, creates the reserve accumulation program, establishes inflation targeting at 5% by 2026, and reforms the Treasury's relationship with the Central Bank. Finance Minister Şimşek and Central Bank Governor Erkan implemented the dramatic policy reversal.
laws.penalty: Criminal sanctions for Central Bank governors deviating from inflation mandate without parliamentary approval
exceptions: Emergency monetary measures during financial crises subject to special oversight
Exchange rate interventions during extreme volatility permitted
laws.sourceLabel: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey

quiz.q: What was Turkey's inflation rate during its unconventional monetary policy period?
quiz.explanation: Turkey experienced inflation exceeding 80% under its unconventional low-interest rate policy, driving the return to monetary orthodoxy.

laws.title: Turkey Earthquake Preparedness and Urban Transformation Act
laws.subtitle: Building Stock Safety and Disaster Resilience Law
laws.fullDescription: Implements massive urban transformation following the devastating February 2023 earthquakes that killed 50,000+ people in Turkey and Syria. The law mandates seismic assessment and upgrading of all high-risk buildings by 2030, creates forced demolition authority for dangerous buildings, establishes state-funded reconstruction for residents displaced by mandatory demolitions, creates contractor liability for buildings that collapse in earthquakes, and reforms building permits with mandatory independent certification.
laws.penalty: Criminal prosecution for engineers and contractors certifying inadequate buildings; up to 15 years for buildings that collapse
exceptions: Historic buildings have specialized conservation-compatible seismic retrofitting
Rural residential buildings under 200 square meters have simplified assessment
laws.sourceLabel: Turkey Ministry of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change

quiz.q: How many people died in Turkey during the February 2023 earthquakes?
quiz.explanation: The devastating February 2023 earthquakes killed over 50,000 people in Turkey and Syria, driving Turkey's building safety and earthquake preparedness reforms.

laws.title: Turkey Istanbul Mayor Imamoglu Arrest and Opposition Crackdown Act
laws.subtitle: Municipal Democracy and Political Prosecution Framework
laws.fullDescription: Documents and responds to the March 2025 arrest of Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu on corruption charges widely seen as politically motivated. The law enacted through court orders establishes the legal framework for prosecuting elected officials, creates interim mayoral appointment mechanisms, and has prompted massive street protests. International observers including EU and US have criticized the prosecutions as undermining Turkish democracy.
laws.penalty: Imprisonment for conviction on corruption charges; suspension from office during prosecution
exceptions: Elected officials retain immunity from arrest while parliamentary majority supports
Administrative court review available for impeachment decisions

quiz.q: Who was arrested in Turkey in March 2025 in a case seen as politically motivated?
quiz.explanation: Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu was arrested in March 2025 on corruption charges widely criticized as politically motivated by the Erdogan government.

laws.title: Turkey F-16 Upgrade and Defense Industry Localization Act
laws.subtitle: NATO Ally Relations and Domestic Arms Industry Law
laws.fullDescription: Manages Turkey's complex NATO relationships through defense procurement and domestic industry development. The law creates the ASELSAN, Roketsan, and TUSAS expansion frameworks, implements the F-16 modernization program secured through NATO diplomacy, establishes the KAAN fifth-generation fighter program, creates export frameworks for Turkish defense products, and establishes defense cooperation frameworks with regional allies.
laws.penalty: Procurement fraud penalties; export control violations for unauthorized defense technology transfer
exceptions: NATO intelligence sharing continues regardless of bilateral disputes
Emergency defense supply from allies during security crisis

quiz.q: What is the name of Turkey's domestically developed fifth-generation fighter jet program?
quiz.explanation: Turkey's KAAN is its domestically developed fifth-generation stealth fighter jet, reducing Turkey's dependence on foreign aircraft.

laws.title: Monetary Policy Normalization Under Erkan and Simsek
laws.subtitle: Turkey Abandons Unorthodox Interest Rate Policy
laws.fullDescription: Turkey finally embraced orthodox monetary policy in 2023-24 following a severe currency crisis, raising interest rates from 8.5% to over 50% under new Finance Minister Mehmet Simsek. The dramatic policy reversal helped stabilize the lira and attract foreign capital, though inflation remained elevated and cost of living pressures continued.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties; market and economic consequences of policy decisions
exceptions: Central bank independence framework
IMF consultation provisions

quiz.q: What dramatic monetary policy change did Turkey make in 2023-24?
options: Raised interest rates from 8.5% to over 50%
