quiz.explanation: Turkey reversed its unorthodox low-interest-rate policy, raising rates dramatically from 8.5% to over 50% under Finance Minister Simsek to combat inflation.

laws.title: Istanbul and Opposition Mayoral Victories
laws.subtitle: CHP Wins Major Cities Despite Erdogan Dominance
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's March 2024 municipal elections saw the opposition CHP party win major cities including Istanbul, Ankara, and Izmir by wide margins, representing a significant rebuke of President Erdogan despite his dominance of national politics. Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu won with an expanded majority, increasing speculation about his presidential ambitions.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties; democratic election outcome
exceptions: Constitutional presidential power remains with Erdogan
Municipal vs. national authority division

quiz.q: Who won re-election as Istanbul mayor in Turkey's 2024 municipal elections?
quiz.explanation: Ekrem Imamoglu of the opposition CHP won re-election as Istanbul mayor with an expanded majority, representing a rebuke of Erdogan despite his national dominance.

laws.title: Kahramanmaras Earthquake Reconstruction
laws.subtitle: Turkey Rebuilds After Deadliest Modern Earthquake
laws.fullDescription: Turkey continued massive reconstruction following the February 6, 2023 Kahramanmaras earthquakes that killed over 50,000 people and destroyed hundreds of thousands of buildings. The government built new housing for hundreds of thousands, prosecuted building code violators, and reformed construction inspection. The disaster became Turkey's largest reconstruction effort.
laws.penalty: Criminal prosecutions for building code violations; fines for illegal construction
exceptions: Emergency construction bypass procedures
Heritage building special provisions

quiz.q: How many people died in Turkey's February 2023 Kahramanmaras earthquakes?
quiz.explanation: Turkey's February 2023 Kahramanmaras earthquakes killed over 50,000 people in Turkey and Syria, triggering massive reconstruction and building code enforcement.

laws.title: Defense Industry Export Growth
laws.subtitle: Turkey Becomes Top 15 Global Defense Exporter
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's defense industry achieved remarkable growth, becoming one of the world's top 15 defense exporters with products including Bayraktar TB2 and Akinci drones, T-129 helicopters, and naval vessels. The TB2 drone's effectiveness in Ukraine, Libya, and Nagorno-Karabakh drove global demand. TUSAS and Roketsan became major exporters.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties; export license compliance
exceptions: Arms embargo restrictions by destination country
NATO ally coordination

quiz.q: What Turkish weapon system became famous for its battlefield effectiveness?
quiz.explanation: The Bayraktar TB2 drone became globally famous for its effectiveness in Ukraine, Libya, and Nagorno-Karabakh, driving Turkey's rise as a top defense exporter.

laws.title: Turkish Lira Crisis and Unconventional Monetary Policy
laws.subtitle: Turkey's inflation crisis and central bank independence battles
laws.fullDescription: Turkey experienced one of the world's worst currency crises with the Turkish lira losing over 80% of its value against the dollar over five years. President Erdoğan's unconventional belief that high interest rates cause inflation led to rate cuts even as inflation exceeded 80%. Eventually, orthodox economists were appointed and interest rates raised dramatically. Turkey's inflation crisis devastated middle-class savings and forced fundamental economic policy changes.
laws.penalty: Foreign currency denominated contracts restricted to prevent dollarization of economy
exceptions: Export contracts can be denominated in foreign currency
International loan agreements maintain foreign currency denomination

laws.title: Erdoğan's Re-election and Opposition Municipality Victories
laws.subtitle: Turkey's political opposition controls major cities despite Erdoğan presidency
laws.fullDescription: Erdoğan won the 2023 presidential election but faces a complicated political landscape where the opposition CHP controls Istanbul, Ankara, and most major cities. Istanbul Mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu became Turkey's most popular opposition figure. The government repeatedly attempted to remove İmamoğlu (arrested in 2025 on politically motivated charges), sparking massive protests. Turkey navigates between NATO membership and strategic relationships with Russia, balancing its role as mediator in the Ukraine conflict with defense cooperation with both sides.
laws.penalty: Opposition mayors face central government financial restrictions that limit their ability to implement policies
exceptions: Municipal responsibilities for water, transport, and waste are constitutionally protected
EU-funded urban development projects continue regardless of central government restrictions on municipalities

laws.title: Middle Corridor Hub and Geopolitical Positioning
laws.subtitle: Turkey leverages Bosphorus control and transit position
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's control of the Bosphorus Strait — through which Russian Black Sea fleet passes — gives it extraordinary leverage. Turkey applied the Montreux Convention to restrict warship passage after Russia's Ukraine invasion. Turkey has positioned itself as a key transit hub for the Middle Corridor (Central Asia to Europe trade route), energy transit from Central Asia, and as a mediator between Russia and Ukraine. Turkey's Bayraktar drones are exported widely and symbolize its defense industry ambitions.
laws.penalty: Montreux Convention requirements for Bosphorus passage are enforced by Turkish maritime authorities
exceptions: Black Sea riparian state warships have different passage rights than non-riparian states
Commercial shipping through the Bosphorus continues under separate international maritime law

quiz.q: What treaty governs Turkey's control of the Bosphorus Strait?
quiz.explanation: The Montreux Convention (1936) gives Turkey the right to regulate warship passage through the Bosphorus — a power Turkey invoked after Russia's invasion of Ukraine to restrict Russian naval movements.

laws.title: Defense Industry Independence and Drone Exports
laws.subtitle: Turkey builds world-class defense industry to reduce NATO dependency
laws.fullDescription: Turkey has invested massively in domestic defense production to reduce dependence on Western arms suppliers (who imposed embargoes after Turkey bought Russian S-400 systems). Baykar's Bayraktar TB2 drone became globally recognized after Ukraine used it to destroy Russian armor. Turkey exports drones to 30+ countries. Turkish warships, armored vehicles, and helicopters are increasingly domestic. Turkey aims for 75%+ domestic defense procurement. The defense industry generates export revenue and technological spillovers.
laws.penalty: Arms exports require government approval; sales to countries under international embargo prohibited
exceptions: Defense research partnerships with allied countries have expedited approval
Dual-use technology exports require separate export control licensing

quiz.q: What conflict made the Bayraktar TB2 drone globally famous?
quiz.explanation: The Bayraktar TB2 gained global attention during Ukraine's defense against Russia's invasion, where it proved highly effective destroying Russian armor and logistics — boosting Turkey's defense export reputation dramatically.

laws.title: Inflation Crisis and Unorthodox Monetary Policy Reversal
laws.subtitle: Turkey's economic turbulence and currency collapse
laws.fullDescription: Turkey experienced one of the world's worst inflation crises among major economies, with consumer price inflation exceeding 85% in 2022 and remaining elevated through 2024. The crisis was precipitated by President Erdogan's insistence on keeping interest rates low despite high inflation — a position contrary to standard monetary economics but driven by Erdogan's stated religious belief that high interest rates cause inflation rather than cure it. The Turkish lira lost over 80% of its value against the dollar over several years. After the 2023 elections, Erdogan appointed orthodox economists including Mehmet Simsek as Finance Minister and allowed the central bank to raise interest rates aggressively, beginning a painful but necessary stabilization. Turkey's economy is diverse and resilient — tourism, automotive manufacturing, textile exports, and agriculture are significant — but the currency crisis devastated household savings and real wages.
laws.penalty: Currency fraud and financial crimes carry criminal penalties; capital controls have been used during currency crisis periods
exceptions: Export-oriented businesses received some preferential treatment for currency holdings
laws.sourceLabel: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey

quiz.q: What was unusual about President Erdogan's stated belief about interest rates?
options: He believed interest rates should be set by referendum
He believed high interest rates cause inflation rather than cure it
He believed interest rates should be pegged to oil prices
He believed interest rates should be eliminated entirely
quiz.explanation: Erdogan stated a belief that high interest rates cause inflation rather than cure it — contrary to standard monetary economics — which led him to insist on low rates even as inflation exceeded 85%, worsening the crisis.

laws.title: Syrian Refugee Crisis and Domestic Political Pressure
laws.subtitle: Turkey hosting the world's largest refugee population
laws.fullDescription: Turkey hosts approximately 3.5-4 million registered Syrian refugees — the world's largest refugee population by country — creating enormous social, economic, and political pressure. The Syrian conflict beginning in 2011 drove millions to flee, and Turkey opened its borders generously initially. Over time, refugee presence has become a major political issue, with significant public resentment particularly during economic difficulties. President Erdogan has used the refugee issue as leverage with the EU, threatening to open borders to Europe. Turkey has pursued voluntary return programs to parts of Syria, including areas controlled by Turkish-backed forces. The Syrian earthquake of 2023, which killed over 50,000 people in Turkey and Syria, reinforced the connection between Turkey's security situation and Syrian instability. Turkey conducts regular military operations in northern Syria targeting Kurdish forces it considers terrorist organizations.
laws.penalty: Refugees have legal status but limited work rights; irregular migration across Turkish borders carries legal consequences
exceptions: UNHCR-recognized refugees have specific legal protections under international refugee law

quiz.q: Approximately how many Syrian refugees does Turkey host — the world's largest refugee population by country?
quiz.explanation: Turkey hosts approximately 3.5-4 million registered Syrian refugees — the world's largest refugee population by country — creating significant social, economic, and political pressure that has shaped Turkish domestic politics.

laws.title: Tourism Powerhouse and Cultural Diplomacy
laws.subtitle: Turkey attracting record tourists through cultural and natural assets
laws.fullDescription: Turkey has become one of the world's top five tourist destinations, receiving over 55 million international visitors annually — a remarkable achievement for a country that faced significant tourism disruptions from terrorism, political instability, and COVID. Istanbul, Cappadocia, the Aegean and Mediterranean coasts, and historical sites including Ephesus, Troy, and Catalhoyuk attract tourists from Europe, Russia, the Gulf States, and increasingly Asia. Turkey's favorable exchange rate (driven by currency depreciation) has made it excellent value for international visitors. The government has actively promoted tourism as an economic pillar, investing in infrastructure and marketing. Turkey has also developed medical tourism, cultural tourism around Ottoman heritage, and adventure tourism. Tourism generates significant foreign exchange earnings critical for Turkey's balance of payments. The country has navigated the Russia-Ukraine war to maintain tourism from both Russian and European markets.
laws.penalty: Tourism regulations require licensing of operators, guides, and accommodation; archaeological site regulations carry significant penalties for violations
exceptions: Private archaeological research requires special permits from Turkish authorities
laws.sourceLabel: Turkish Ministry of Culture and Tourism

quiz.q: Approximately how many international tourists does Turkey receive annually?
quiz.explanation: Turkey receives over 55 million international tourists annually, making it one of the world's top five tourist destinations, with Istanbul, Cappadocia, and the coastal regions attracting visitors from across Europe, Russia, and the Gulf States.

laws.title: Imamoglu Arrest and Opposition Crackdown
laws.subtitle: Istanbul mayor jailed before expected presidential run
laws.fullDescription: Ekrem İmamoğlu, the popular Istanbul mayor and leading opposition challenger to Erdoğan, was arrested in March 2025 on terrorism and corruption charges widely seen as politically motivated. The arrest triggered massive protests across Turkey, the largest since the Gezi Park protests of 2013. İmamoğlu had been expected to challenge Erdoğan in future elections. European governments condemned the arrest. İmamoğlu won the Istanbul mayoral election while imprisoned. The case represented the starkest use of judicial power against political opposition in modern Turkish history.
laws.penalty: Mayors can be removed from office by Interior Ministry while facing criminal charges; assets frozen during investigation
exceptions: Constitutional protections require court processes even in politically sensitive cases
European Convention on Human Rights applies to Turkey

quiz.q: What position did Ekrem İmamoğlu hold when he was arrested in March 2025?
quiz.explanation: Ekrem İmamoğlu was the Mayor of Istanbul when he was arrested in March 2025 on charges widely seen as politically motivated to prevent him from challenging Erdoğan in future elections.

laws.title: Social Media Law and Platform Penalties
laws.subtitle: Turkey forces global tech giants to comply with content removal
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's social media law requires platforms with more than one million daily users to appoint local representatives, store Turkish user data locally and respond to content removal requests within 48 hours. Non-compliant platforms face bandwidth throttling of up to 90%—effectively making them unusable. Twitter/X, YouTube and others complied after initially being throttled. The law has been used extensively to remove content critical of the government and to limit coverage of disasters, corruption allegations and protests.
laws.penalty: Non-compliant platforms face 90% bandwidth throttling; fines up to 30 million Turkish lira
exceptions: International news organizations have some journalistic protections
Academic research on platform content subject to different standards
laws.sourceLabel: Information Technologies and Communication Authority of Turkey

quiz.q: What does Turkey's social media law require platforms to do within 48 hours of government requests?
quiz.explanation: Turkey's social media law requires platforms to remove content within 48 hours of government requests, backed by the threat of 90% bandwidth throttling that effectively makes platforms unusable—forcing global tech companies to comply.

laws.title: Inflation Shock and Orthodox Policy Return
laws.subtitle: Turkey reverses Erdoğan's unorthodox monetary policy under crisis
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's inflation soared above 80% under Erdoğan's unorthodox theory that high interest rates cause inflation, leading him to cut rates despite rising prices. After the 2023 election, Erdoğan appointed new economic team members including Mehmet Şimşek as finance minister who reversed course, dramatically raising interest rates. Inflation began declining from its peaks. Turkey's lira had lost over 80% of its value against the dollar in a few years. The return to monetary orthodoxy was politically difficult but economically necessary.
laws.penalty: Central Bank's monetary policy now independent in practice; interest rate decisions made on orthodox economic principles
exceptions: State bank lending to priority sectors continues at subsidized rates
Export finance programs maintain favorable rates for exporters

quiz.q: What unorthodox theory did Erdoğan apply that caused Turkey's inflation to soar above 80%?
options: That high interest rates cause inflation, so he cut rates despite rising prices
quiz.explanation: Erdoğan's unorthodox belief that high interest rates cause inflation (the opposite of mainstream economics) led him to cut rates as inflation rose, causing Turkey's lira to collapse and inflation to exceed 80% before he reversed course after the 2023 election.

laws.title: Turkish Climate Law and Paris Agreement Ratification
laws.subtitle: Late Ratifier, High Vulnerability
laws.fullDescription: Turkey ratified the Paris Agreement only in October 2021 — years after most nations — and submitted a target to reach net zero emissions by 2053. Turkey is among the world's top 20 emitters and has one of the fastest-growing carbon footprints. Despite ratification, Turkey continues expanding coal capacity. Climate vulnerability is high: the 2021 Manavgat wildfires and Black Sea floods occurred within days of each other, killing hundreds. Turkey's Black Sea coast, fertile agricultural heartland, and Mediterranean coastline face severe climate risks.
laws.penalty: New Environmental Law (2021) increases fines significantly; environmental impact assessments mandatory
exceptions: Coal expansion under 'energy security' justification
Agricultural emissions under developing country framework

laws.title: Universal Health Insurance and Health Transformation Program
laws.subtitle: Rapid Healthcare Expansion
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Health Transformation Program (2003-2011) under Health Minister Erdoğan dramatically improved healthcare access: establishing universal health insurance (Genel Sağlık Sigortası), a family medicine system placing primary care doctors in every neighborhood, and massive hospital construction. Turkey built 'city hospitals' — mega-hospital campuses with 1,000-3,000 beds. Life expectancy improved significantly. Universal health insurance covers all legal residents from the state budget if not covered by employment. Turkey has become a medical tourism destination for procedures including hair transplants and dental care.
laws.penalty: All legal residents must be covered by health insurance; state covers those without employer coverage; fines for employers failing to register workers
exceptions: Refugees and asylum seekers have limited access under UNHCR framework
Complementary private insurance for faster access to private hospitals

laws.title: Turkish Labor Law and Minimum Wage
laws.subtitle: World's Highest Minimum Wage Increase
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Labor Law No. 4857 provides comprehensive worker protections: severance pay, notice periods, annual leave (14-26 days depending on tenure), and overtime restrictions. Turkey dramatically raised its minimum wage — from TL 4,250 (Jan 2022) to TL 22,104 (Jan 2024) — a nominal increase of over 400% due to extreme inflation. Turkish unions have historically been weak due to high thresholds for strike votes and restrictions on political strikes. Erdoğan's government has at times banned strikes in key sectors citing 'national security.' Turkey has significant informal employment (~35%).
laws.penalty: Labor Law violations: Work Inspectorate fines; illegal dismissal: severance mandatory; union interference: criminal liability
exceptions: Seasonal agricultural workers under different framework
Domestic workers have special protections

laws.title: Turkey YÖK University System and Religious Education
laws.subtitle: Imam Hatip Schools Rise
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's YÖK (Council of Higher Education) oversees all universities. University admission is through the YKS national exam. Turkey has dramatically expanded higher education — from 27 universities in 1984 to 208 today. Turkey's AKP government significantly expanded Imam Hatip (religious vocation) schools from a small minority to 10%+ of students, reflecting the ruling party's Islamist orientation. Turkey has faced significant tensions over university autonomy — Boğaziçi University protests (2021) when the government appointed a controversial rector sparked nationwide demonstrations.
laws.penalty: YÖK exercises strong oversight; professors face dismissal for political activity; private schools must register with MEB
exceptions: Minority schools (Armenian, Greek, Jewish) under special treaties
Foreign language schools under bilateral agreements

laws.title: World's Largest Refugee Host Law
laws.subtitle: Turkey's hosting of 3.5 million Syrian refugees
laws.fullDescription: Turkey hosts more refugees than any country globally — approximately 3.5-4 million Syrians plus hundreds of thousands from Afghanistan, Iraq, and other countries. Turkey's Law on Foreigners and International Protection (2013) established a modern refugee framework replacing Ottoman-era laws. Syrian refugees receive 'Temporary Protection Status' rather than full refugee status under the 1951 Convention (which Turkey only applies to Europeans). Turkey has threatened to 'open the gates' to Europe in diplomatic disputes. Integration is limited, with refugees in poor working conditions and many in informal economy.
laws.penalty: Irregular migrants may be detained in removal centers; employers of undocumented workers face fines; human trafficking is a serious criminal offense; refugees found outside their registered province face detention
exceptions: Syrians have Temporary Protection Status allowing work permits
Europeans are full 1951 Convention refugees under Turkey's geographic limitation
laws.sourceLabel: Turkey Law on Foreigners and International Protection (2013)

quiz.q: Turkey hosts approximately how many Syrian refugees, making it the world's largest refugee-hosting country?
quiz.explanation: Turkey hosts approximately 3.5-4 million Syrian refugees (exact numbers fluctuate), far more than any other country, having kept its borders open during the Syrian civil war and providing temporary protection status to Syrians since 2013.

laws.title: Narcotic Drugs Law
laws.subtitle: Turkey's strict drug penalties and cannabis debates
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Narcotic Drugs Law (2313) and Criminal Code impose severe penalties for drug trafficking. Turkey is a major transit country for Afghan heroin moving to Europe and for precursor chemicals for synthetic drugs. Drug trafficking carries 10-20 years imprisonment. Personal use and possession are criminal offenses but may be diverted to treatment for first offenses. Turkey has debated cannabis policy in recent years. Turkey's cannabis eradication programs in eastern regions have been ongoing for decades. Under Erdoğan, no liberalization has occurred.
laws.penalty: Personal use: 1-2 years (may be suspended for treatment); possession: criminal offense with mandatory treatment option; trafficking: 10-20 years; organized trafficking: 15-20 years; facilitating drug use of minors: enhanced penalties
exceptions: First-time personal use may be diverted to compulsory treatment
Medical use of certain narcotics (opioids) with prescription permitted
Industrial hemp cultivation in limited licensed areas

quiz.q: Turkey is a major transit point for which drug traveling from Afghanistan to Europe?
quiz.explanation: Turkey has historically been the primary transit route for Afghan heroin moving from Afghanistan through Iran, Turkey, and the Balkans to Western Europe — the 'Balkan Route.' Turkey seizes significant heroin quantities annually despite serving as a transit country.

laws.title: No Legal Recognition — Pride Banned Since 2015
laws.subtitle: Turkey offers no legal recognition for same-sex relationships and bans Pride marches
laws.fullDescription: Turkey does not recognize same-sex partnerships or marriage, and homosexuality carries significant social stigma despite being technically legal since the Ottoman-era penal code reform of 1858 (and maintained in the Republic since 1923). Since 2015, Istanbul Pride has been banned citing 'public order' concerns, with police using tear gas and rubber pellets against marchers. Trans people face particular violence and discrimination. Transgender identity is not legally recognized without invasive surgery requirements. The AKP government under Erdoğan has increasingly used anti-LGBTQ+ rhetoric.
laws.penalty: No legal protections against discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity; LGBTQ+ activists face legal harassment
exceptions: Private same-sex conduct between adults is not criminalized

quiz.q: Since what year has Istanbul Pride been banned in Turkey?
quiz.explanation: Istanbul Pride was banned starting in 2015, with authorities citing public order concerns. Police have used force against participants in subsequent years, reversing a decade of previously permitted events.

laws.title: World's Largest Jailer of Journalists
laws.subtitle: Turkey has held the record for most imprisoned journalists globally for many years
laws.fullDescription: Turkey regularly holds or contends for the title of world's largest jailer of journalists. Dozens of journalists are imprisoned at any given time, primarily under broad anti-terrorism and sedition laws. The 2016 coup attempt led to a massive crackdown: hundreds of media outlets were closed, thousands of press credentials revoked, and numerous journalists arrested. Turkey's broad definitions of 'terrorism' allow prosecution of virtually any critical reporting. Self-censorship is pervasive. Foreign correspondents face visa restrictions and deportation. Turkey ranks near the bottom globally for press freedom.
laws.penalty: Criminal prosecution under anti-terrorism laws; journalists face years in pre-trial detention; outlets can be shut by decree
exceptions: Some independent online media continues to operate despite severe pressure

quiz.q: What legal tool does Turkey primarily use to prosecute and imprison journalists?
quiz.explanation: Turkey primarily uses broad anti-terrorism and sedition laws to prosecute journalists — laws with definitions so expansive that virtually any critical reporting on the government, Kurdish issues, or security forces can be deemed 'terrorism support' or 'espionage.'

laws.title: Social Media Law — Forced Local Representatives and Bandwidth Throttling
laws.subtitle: Turkey forced social media platforms to appoint local representatives or face bandwidth cuts
laws.fullDescription: Turkey passed Social Media Law No. 7253 (2020) requiring social media platforms with more than 1 million Turkish daily users to appoint a local representative, store Turkish user data in Turkey, and respond to content removal requests within 48 hours. Platforms that did not comply faced advertising bans and 90% bandwidth throttling (effectively making them unusable). YouTube, Twitter/X, Facebook, TikTok, and others initially refused but ultimately complied after their traffic was throttled. Turkey also blocks specific content on platforms, including coverage critical of the government, Atatürk insults, and Kurdish-related content.
laws.penalty: 90% bandwidth throttling for non-compliance; advertising bans; content removal requirements within 48 hours
exceptions: Platforms complying with representative requirements can operate

quiz.q: What leverage did Turkey use to force social media platforms to comply with its local representative law?
options: 90% bandwidth throttling making platforms effectively unusable
Blocking Turkish users from signing up
quiz.explanation: Turkey used 90% bandwidth throttling as leverage — slowing platforms to the point of being effectively unusable — to force major social media companies including YouTube, Twitter/X, and Facebook to comply with Social Media Law No. 7253 requiring local representatives and Turkish data storage.

laws.title: BDDK Banking Regulation & Lira Stability Measures
laws.subtitle: Turkey restricts crypto trading and enforces lira use amid currency volatility
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Banking Regulation and Supervision Agency (BDDK/Bankacılık Düzenleme ve Denetleme Kurumu) oversees all banking operations. In 2021, Turkey banned the use of cryptocurrencies for payments, citing risks to financial stability amid 80%+ annual inflation. While crypto trading remains legal on exchanges, merchants cannot accept crypto as payment. BDDK imposed restrictions on Turkish banks lending to foreign companies holding large lira positions (a measure to prevent short-selling of the lira). The Capital Markets Board (SPK) also regulates crypto asset service providers under new 2024 legislation requiring licenses.
laws.penalty: Using crypto for payments: fines up to ₺1 million; operating unlicensed crypto exchange: up to 5 years imprisonment; currency manipulation: severe criminal penalties
exceptions: Crypto exchanges licensed under SPK rules may operate
Cross-border trade invoiced in foreign currency is permitted
Tourists may use foreign payment cards without restriction

quiz.q: What did Turkey ban in 2021 regarding cryptocurrency?
options: Using crypto as payment for goods and services
quiz.explanation: Turkey banned the use of cryptocurrencies as a payment method in April 2021, though trading on exchanges remained legal. The ban aimed to protect financial stability amid severe lira depreciation.

laws.title: TGDF Food Codex & Turkish Culinary Heritage Rules
laws.subtitle: Turkey's food standards protect traditional products and regulate its massive agri-food sector
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's food safety system involves multiple agencies: the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry (GTHB) for production and the Ministry of Health for consumer protection. Turkey's Turkish Food Codex (TGDF) sets standards for all food products. Turkey is a major agricultural producer — world's largest producer of figs, apricots, cherries, and hazelnuts. Turkish hazelnut production regulations (Turkey supplies ~70% of world hazelnuts) include pesticide limits and quality standards important for European confectionery companies (Nutella uses Turkish hazelnuts). Turkey has geographical indications for products like Antep Baklavası (Gaziantep baklava, GI), Maraş Dondurması (elastic Kahramanmaraş ice cream), and Urfa Biber (peppers).
laws.penalty: Turkish Food Codex violations: administrative fines up to TRY 500,000; food fraud: criminal prosecution; exporting substandard agricultural products: export suspension and fines
exceptions: Traditional village food production for local consumption has modified oversight
Religious holiday food preparations (Ramadan, Eid) at community level have cultural exemptions
Small artisan producers of traditional sweets have simplified licensing

quiz.q: What percentage of the world's hazelnuts does Turkey produce, making its food safety standards globally significant?
quiz.explanation: Turkey produces approximately 70% of the world's hazelnuts, primarily from the Black Sea coast. This dominance means Turkish hazelnut quality standards and pesticide regulations directly affect global confectionery supply chains — including major products like Nutella and countless chocolates worldwide.

laws.title: Turkey Animal Protection Law — Stray Dog Controversy 2024
laws.subtitle: Turkey's 2024 law mandating stray dog euthanasia sparked national debate
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Law 5199 (Animal Protection Law, 2004) was amended significantly in 2024 (Law 7511). The 2024 amendment required municipalities to collect stray dogs from streets and house them in shelters — but if shelters are full and no adoption occurs within 30 days, euthanasia is permitted. This was a dramatic reversal from the previous no-kill policy and sparked massive protests across Turkey. Turkey has an estimated 4 million stray dogs. Animal welfare groups argue the law will lead to mass killings; municipalities argue stray dog attacks (including fatal incidents) require action. The 2024 amendment remains deeply controversial and subject to constitutional challenge.
laws.penalty: Animal cruelty: up to 4 years imprisonment (amended 2022); organized cruelty: up to 6 years; abandonment: fines; businesses: licence revocation
exceptions: Livestock farming
Licensed hunting
Scientific research
Working dogs in agriculture

quiz.q: What controversial change did Turkey's 2024 amendment to its Animal Protection Law make regarding stray dogs?
options: It banned all stray dog sterilization
It permitted euthanasia of stray dogs in full shelters after 30 days without adoption
It required all strays to be sent to rural areas
It mandated microchipping of all strays
quiz.explanation: Turkey's controversial 2024 amendment allowed municipalities to euthanize stray dogs when shelters are full and no adoption occurs within 30 days — reversing the previous no-kill policy and sparking massive nationwide protests from animal welfare groups.

laws.title: Turkey Family Law — Civil Code and Erdogan Era Restrictions
laws.subtitle: Turkey's civil code is progressive but Erdogan era reverses some gains
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Civil Code (Medeni Kanun, 2001) was a modernizing reform — it ended the husband's legal status as head of household, established equal property rights for spouses, and introduced a new family law framework. However, since the AKP government under Erdogan, several family law concerns have emerged: Turkey withdrew from the Istanbul Convention on Violence Against Women in 2021 (by presidential decree), facing massive domestic and international criticism. Turkey's Civil Code uses 'edinilmiş mallara katılma rejimi' (participation in acquired goods) as the default regime. Turkey has a significant Sharia-based marriage (imam nikahı — imam's blessing) parallel practice in rural areas, though only civil marriage is legally valid.
laws.penalty: Civil enforcement through aile mahkemeleri (family courts); nafaka (alimony/support) enforcement; criminal penalties for domestic violence under TCK 86
exceptions: Mal ayrılığı (separation of property) by premarital agreement
Pre-marital property retained
Imam marriages — not legally recognized but widely practiced

quiz.q: What controversial family law action did Turkey's Erdogan government take in 2021?
options: Turkey withdrew from the Istanbul Convention on Violence Against Women by presidential decree
Turkey required religious marriage in addition to civil marriage
quiz.explanation: In March 2021, President Erdogan withdrew Turkey from the Istanbul Convention (the Council of Europe's landmark treaty on preventing violence against women) by presidential decree overnight — causing massive protests in Turkey and international condemnation. Turkey became the first country to withdraw from the treaty.

laws.title: Turkey Kira Artis Siniri & Property Rights
laws.subtitle: Rent increase limits and urban transformation law
laws.fullDescription: Turkey implemented emergency rent increase caps (Law 7409/2022) limiting increases to 25% annually during 2022-2024, then transitioning to a 12-month average CPI benchmark, responding to 80%+ inflation. The Kentsel Donusum (Urban Transformation) Law 6306/2012 allows compulsory acquisition of 'risky buildings' for earthquake-preparedness reconstruction, affecting millions of buildings in Istanbul and other earthquake-prone areas. Foreign nationals from eligible countries can purchase property in Turkey, and this has been a significant source of investment, particularly from Russia, Iran, and Gulf states following various geopolitical events.
laws.penalty: Rent above legal cap: tenant can apply to dispute commission; urban transformation: mandatory relocation with temporary accommodation
exceptions: Inflation exceeding 80% in 2022 prompted emergency rent caps
Urban transformation law targets seismically risky buildings
laws.sourceLabel: Turkey Rent Cap & Urban Transformation Law

quiz.q: What emergency measure did Turkey implement in 2022-2024 regarding rent increases due to high inflation?
quiz.explanation: Turkey's Law 7409 (2022) imposed an emergency cap of 25% on annual residential rent increases, responding to inflation that exceeded 80% in 2022 and was causing massive housing affordability crises for renters.

laws.title: Turkey Tuketicinin Korunmasi Hakkinda Kanun
laws.subtitle: Consumer protection law with active enforcement
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Law on Consumer Protection (No. 6502/2013) provides comprehensive protections including 14-day withdrawal right for distance purchases, 2-year warranty with mandatory reversal of burden of proof, and regulation of consumer loans and credit cards. The Ministry of Commerce and Consumer Protection Directorate enforce the law. The Tuketici Hakem Heyetleri (Consumer Arbitration Committees) at the district level handle disputes up to TRY 300,000 without cost. Consumer associations (TUKODER) are active. Turkey has specific protections on subscription cancellation rights and doorstep sales. High inflation in 2022-2023 prompted emergency consumer price monitoring measures.
laws.penalty: Consumer law violation: administrative fines from TRY 1,000 to 5 million; warranty: repair/replace within 20 days
exceptions: Consumer Arbitration Committees: free dispute resolution up to TRY 300,000
Emergency price monitoring implemented during 2022-2023 inflation crisis

quiz.q: What free dispute resolution system does Turkey use for consumer claims at the district level?
options: The Administrative Courts at no cost
quiz.explanation: Turkey's Tuketici Hakem Heyetleri (Consumer Arbitration Committees) operate at the district level and handle consumer disputes up to TRY 300,000 completely free of charge — providing accessible justice for consumers without requiring expensive lawyers or court fees.

laws.title: Presidential Government System
laws.subtitle: Constitutional changes from parliamentary to presidential rule
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's April 2017 constitutional referendum, approved by 51.4% of voters, abolished the office of Prime Minister and transitioned to a presidential system effective from June 2018. Under the new system, President Erdoğan exercises executive power directly, appointing and dismissing ministers, vice presidents, and senior judges without parliamentary approval. The president can issue decrees with force of law in areas not explicitly reserved for parliament. Critics including the Venice Commission of the Council of Europe warned the changes created insufficient checks on executive power and undermined judicial independence.
laws.penalty: Violations of presidential decrees treated as administrative offenses; penalties vary by subject matter of decree
exceptions: Parliamentary oversight of budget remains constitutionally guaranteed
Constitutional amendments still require parliamentary supermajority and referendum
International treaties require parliamentary ratification

quiz.q: What percentage of Turkish voters approved the 2017 constitutional referendum establishing a presidential system?
quiz.explanation: The April 2017 referendum was approved by 51.4% of voters, a narrow margin that reflected deep polarization over concentrating executive power in the presidency.

laws.title: Press Freedom Restrictions and Media Law
laws.subtitle: Anti-terrorism provisions used against journalists
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Anti-Terror Law (Law 3713/1991 as amended) and Article 314 of the Turkish Penal Code on armed organization membership have been extensively used to prosecute journalists, with Turkey regularly ranking among the top countries for imprisoned journalists according to CPJ and RSF indices. The 2016 emergency decree laws (KHK) shut down over 150 media outlets and revoked press credentials of thousands of journalists. The Radio and Television Supreme Council (RTÜK) has authority to suspend broadcast licenses for content deemed threatening to national security or public order. Defamation of the president under Article 299 carries up to 4 years imprisonment.
laws.penalty: Anti-terror charges: 7.5 years to life imprisonment; Presidential insult (Art.299): up to 4 years; RTÜK suspension: 1-5 day broadcast ban to license revocation
exceptions: Parliamentary immunity protects deputies' legislative speech
Academic publications enjoy limited protection under freedom of science
Foreign correspondent accreditation provides partial procedural protections

quiz.q: Which Turkish legal provision criminalizing presidential insult carries up to 4 years imprisonment?
quiz.explanation: Article 299 of the Turkish Penal Code criminalizes insulting the President of the Republic, carrying up to 4 years imprisonment, frequently applied against journalists and social media users.

laws.title: LGBTQ+ Pride Parade Ban in Istanbul
laws.subtitle: Restriction of public assembly for sexual minority groups
laws.fullDescription: Istanbul's governor's office has banned the annual Pride March since 2015, citing public order and security concerns, after the event had been held peacefully for over a decade. Turkish authorities have used Law 2911 on Meetings and Demonstrations to disperse attendees with rubber bullets and tear gas. The Council of State (Danıştay) upheld the ban in 2019, ruling it compatible with public safety requirements. Similar bans have been extended to Ankara and other cities. Turkey removed LGBT-related content from school curricula and President Erdoğan has made anti-LGBTQ+ rhetoric central to political messaging, framing it as protection of family values.
laws.penalty: Participation in banned assemblies: fines and detention up to 3 years for organizers; dispersal by force for attendees
exceptions: Private gatherings on private property not covered by assembly law
Academic conferences on gender issues retain limited protection
Online expression not yet criminalized under specific LGBT provisions

quiz.q: In what year did Istanbul authorities first ban the annual Pride March?
quiz.explanation: Istanbul's governor's office first banned the Pride March in 2015, after the event had been held peacefully since 2003; police have used force to disperse attendees at subsequent attempted marches.

laws.title: Internet Content Blocking and Social Media Law
laws.subtitle: Law 5651 and social media platform restrictions
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Law 5651 on Internet Publications has been amended multiple times to expand government blocking powers, most recently in 2022 to require social media platforms with over 1 million daily users to appoint local representatives and store Turkish user data domestically. Platforms failing to comply face advertising bans and bandwidth throttling of 50% then 90%. Turkey has blocked Wikipedia for nearly 3 years (2017-2020), and temporarily restricted Twitter, Facebook, and YouTube multiple times during political crises. The Information and Communication Technologies Authority (BTK) can order content removal within 4 hours for privacy violations and 24 hours for other categories.
laws.penalty: Platforms without local representative: advertising ban then 50%-90% bandwidth reduction; individual content creators: fines and criminal charges
exceptions: Encrypted communications (VPN) technically legal but discouraged
Academic and research networks (ULAKNET) have separate access arrangements
News agencies with press accreditation have expedited appeals process

quiz.q: How long did Turkey block Wikipedia under Law 5651?
quiz.explanation: Turkey blocked Wikipedia from April 2017 to December 2020 — nearly 3 years — under Law 5651, citing content it deemed insulting to the Turkish state.

laws.title: Kurdish Political Representation and HDP Closure Case
laws.subtitle: Constitutional Court proceedings against pro-Kurdish party
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Constitutional Court initiated closure proceedings against the Peoples' Democratic Party (HDP), the main pro-Kurdish political party, in 2021 based on alleged links to the PKK (Kurdistan Workers' Party). The case, if successful, would bar over 400 politicians from politics for up to 5 years and seize party assets. The HDP rebranded as HEDEP and then DEM Party in anticipation of potential closure. Turkey has previously closed 28 Kurdish political parties since 1993. The European Court of Human Rights and European Commission have criticized the proceedings as disproportionate restrictions on political pluralism.
laws.penalty: Party dissolution: seizure of all party assets; individual bans from political activity for named party members for 5 years
exceptions: Elected deputies retain parliamentary mandate until end of term even if party dissolved
Former members not named in indictment may join other parties
European Court of Human Rights provides external appellate avenue

quiz.q: How many Kurdish political parties has Turkey closed since 1993 prior to the HDP case?
quiz.explanation: Turkey has closed 28 Kurdish political parties since 1993, reflecting the ongoing legal conflict between the state and pro-Kurdish political movements.

laws.title: Renewable Energy Licensing Law
laws.subtitle: YEKDEM support mechanism for wind and solar
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Renewable Energy Law (Law 5346/2005) and its YEKDEM feed-in tariff mechanism, updated in 2021 with the YEKA model for competitive tender, govern the licensing and support of renewable energy projects. Turkey has set targets of 60% renewable electricity by 2035. Renewable energy projects require Environmental Impact Assessment approval from the Ministry of Environment and licenses from the Energy Market Regulatory Authority (EPDK). Turkey's wind energy capacity exceeded 12 GW in 2023, with solar rapidly expanding due to favorable irradiation conditions, particularly in the Konya and Karapınar solar zones.
laws.penalty: Operating without energy license: fines up to 1 million TRY; operating without environmental permit: suspension and remediation costs
exceptions: Installations under 1 MW exempt from generation license requirement
Self-consumption solar panels on rooftops follow simplified notification procedure
Municipal energy cooperatives benefit from reduced licensing requirements

quiz.q: What renewable electricity percentage target has Turkey set for 2035?
quiz.explanation: Turkey has set a target of achieving 60% renewable electricity generation by 2035, backed by the YEKA competitive tender system for wind and solar projects.

laws.title: Temporary Protection Regulation for Syrian Refugees
laws.subtitle: Mass refugee protection framework under Cabinet Decision 2013/5149
laws.fullDescription: Turkey hosts the world's largest refugee population, with approximately 3.5 million registered Syrians under the Temporary Protection Regulation enacted by Cabinet Decision 2013/5149 following the Syrian civil war. Temporary Protection status grants access to healthcare, education, and the labor market (with work permit) but does not confer the full rights of refugee status under the 1951 Geneva Convention. Turkey maintains a geographic limitation to the Convention, granting full refugee status only to Europeans. The EU-Turkey Statement of March 2016 provides Turkey with €6 billion in exchange for controlling irregular migration flows to Greek islands.
laws.penalty: Irregular residence by non-protected foreigners: administrative detention; deportation; 5-year entry ban
exceptions: Syrians under Temporary Protection cannot be collectively deported
Unaccompanied children subject to special protection procedures
Marriage to Turkish citizen provides alternative residency pathway
laws.sourceLabel: Turkish Directorate General of Migration Management

quiz.q: Approximately how many registered Syrian refugees does Turkey host under Temporary Protection?
quiz.explanation: Turkey hosts approximately 3.5 million registered Syrians under the Temporary Protection framework — the world's largest refugee population — following the Syrian civil war.

laws.title: Turkish Labor Law and Collective Bargaining
laws.subtitle: Law 6356 on trade unions and collective agreements
laws.fullDescription: Turkish Law 6356/2012 on Trade Unions and Collective Labour Agreements governs worker organizing and collective bargaining, requiring unions to represent at least 1% of workers in a sector and 40% of employees in a specific workplace to obtain bargaining authority. These double-threshold requirements have been criticized by the ILO Committee on Freedom of Association as excessively restrictive. Public sector workers were granted limited collective bargaining rights in 2010 but are prohibited from striking. Turkey has the lowest trade union density in the OECD at approximately 12%, partly attributed to the restrictive threshold requirements.
laws.penalty: Organizing without proper certification: union activities deemed illegal; employer interference in union organization: fines and criminal charges
exceptions: Civil servants may join unions but cannot strike or bargain over wages
Works councils in EU-standard multinational companies operate parallel to union structure
Solidarity strikes permitted under defined conditions
laws.sourceLabel: Turkish Ministry of Labour and Social Security

quiz.q: What minimum workplace representation threshold must Turkish unions achieve to obtain collective bargaining authority?
quiz.explanation: Under Law 6356/2012, Turkish unions must represent at least 40% of employees in a specific workplace to obtain collective bargaining authority — a threshold the ILO considers overly restrictive.

laws.title: Capital Markets Law and Crypto Asset Regulation
laws.subtitle: Law 7518/2024 on crypto assets under CMB oversight
laws.fullDescription: Turkey enacted Law 7518 in July 2024, bringing crypto asset service providers under the Capital Markets Board (SPK) regulatory framework for the first time. The law requires exchanges operating in Turkey to obtain SPK licenses, maintain capital adequacy, segregate client assets, and comply with anti-money laundering requirements. Turkey had one of the world's highest rates of crypto adoption as a hedge against inflation (which reached 85% in 2022) and currency depreciation. Unregulated providers must either obtain licenses or cease operations within six months of the law's effective date.
laws.penalty: Operating unlicensed crypto exchange: criminal charges with 3-5 years imprisonment; market manipulation: up to 7 years imprisonment
exceptions: Token issuers with fewer than 150 investors exempt from full prospectus requirements
Mining operations separate from exchange regulation
Blockchain infrastructure providers distinct from asset service providers

quiz.q: What economic condition drove Turkey's exceptionally high rate of cryptocurrency adoption?
quiz.explanation: Turkey's crypto adoption was driven largely by currency depreciation and inflation that reached 85% in 2022, pushing citizens toward digital assets as an inflation hedge.

laws.title: Tobacco Control and Plain Packaging Law
laws.subtitle: Comprehensive tobacco restrictions under Law 4207
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Law 4207/1996 on the Control of Tobacco Products and Their Harmful Effects has been amended multiple times to implement increasingly strict tobacco controls, including a comprehensive indoor smoking ban since 2009. Turkey introduced graphic health warnings covering 65% of packaging and banned tobacco advertising including point-of-sale displays. E-cigarettes and heated tobacco products are regulated as tobacco products subject to the same restrictions. Turkey ratified the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control in 2004. Smoking rates, while declining, remain high at approximately 28% of adults, above the OECD average.
laws.penalty: Smoking in prohibited areas: fines 69-276 TRY; selling to minors: fines and license suspension; tobacco advertising: fines up to 1 million TRY
exceptions: Designated outdoor smoking areas in specific venue types
Research with ethical committee approval
Traditional tobacco use in cultural contexts not covered by advertising ban

quiz.q: What percentage of cigarette packaging must be covered by graphic health warnings in Turkey?
quiz.explanation: Turkish law requires graphic health warnings covering at least 65% of tobacco product packaging, in line with WHO FCTC implementation recommendations.

laws.title: Counter-Terrorism Law and Emergency Powers
laws.subtitle: Post-2016 coup attempt emergency decree legacy laws
laws.fullDescription: Following the July 2016 attempted coup, Turkey declared a two-year state of emergency during which over 150,000 people were arrested or suspended by emergency decree laws (KHK). The emergency ended in 2018, but the Anti-Terror Law (Law 3713) was amended to incorporate expanded detention powers and the definition of terrorist membership was broadened to include using ByLock encryption app (designated as PKK/Gülenist tool) or having Bank Asya accounts. The Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International documented systematic torture allegations in post-coup detention facilities. Over 2,000 cases were brought before the European Court of Human Rights.
laws.penalty: Membership in terrorist organization: 7.5 years to aggravated life imprisonment; financing terrorism: 5-10 years; propaganda: 1-5 years
exceptions: Journalists and academics retain formal legal protection subject to proportionality
Statutory inquiries commission (Olağanüstü Hal İşlemleri İnceleme Komisyonu) reviews KHK dismissals
European Court of Human Rights provides external remedy avenue

quiz.q: What digital evidence was used to designate individuals as Gülenist terrorist members after 2016?
quiz.explanation: Turkish prosecutors used the presence of the ByLock encrypted messaging app on a person's phone as evidence of Gülenist terrorist organization (FETÖ) membership after the 2016 coup attempt.

laws.title: Central Bank Independence Restrictions
laws.subtitle: Presidential influence over monetary policy
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Central Bank Law was amended in 2017 and 2019 to give the president power to appoint and dismiss the Central Bank governor, a power exercised multiple times — four governors were replaced in rapid succession between 2019 and 2021. The unconventional monetary policy of maintaining low interest rates despite high inflation (the 'Erdoğan Economics' model) led to the Turkish lira losing 80% of its value against the dollar between 2018 and 2023. After the 2023 elections, a more orthodox monetary policy team under Governor Erkan and then Karahan raised rates from 8.5% to 45% to combat 85% inflation.
laws.penalty: Unauthorized foreign currency transactions by individuals: fines; corporate violations of currency regulations: significant administrative penalties
exceptions: Export earnings can be held in foreign currency accounts
Tourism businesses may price in foreign currency
Import payments exempt from local currency conversion requirements
laws.sourceLabel: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey

quiz.q: By approximately what percentage did the Turkish lira depreciate against the dollar between 2018 and 2023?
quiz.explanation: The Turkish lira lost approximately 80% of its value against the US dollar between 2018 and 2023, driven by unconventional low-interest-rate monetary policy pursued by the Erdoğan government.

laws.title: Religious Education Requirements in Schools
laws.subtitle: Compulsory Quran and imam hatip school expansion
laws.fullDescription: Turkey made Quran courses and Prophet's life courses available from 1st grade in public schools under 2012 education reforms, while expanding the imam hatip (religious vocational) school network to over 1.5 million students. Religious Culture and Knowledge of Ethics remains compulsory through high school. The Turkish education system was transformed by a 4+4+4 structure reform in 2012 that controversially extended compulsory education while allowing early transfer to religious vocational tracks. The European Court of Human Rights ruled in Mansur Yalçın v. Turkey (2014) that Turkey violated religious freedom by not providing adequate exemptions from religious education.
laws.penalty: Truancy from compulsory education: fines for parents; schools failing curriculum requirements: closure and loss of accreditation
exceptions: Non-Muslim minority schools (Greek, Armenian, Jewish) follow alternative curricula
Exemption requests from mandatory religious education allowed in principle but difficult in practice
Home schooling not legally recognized

quiz.q: What European court ruled Turkey violated religious freedom through its compulsory religious education policy?
quiz.explanation: The European Court of Human Rights ruled in Mansur Yalçın v. Turkey (2014) that Turkey's compulsory religious education without adequate exemptions violated freedom of religion.

laws.title: Urban Transformation Law and Earthquake Preparedness
laws.subtitle: Law 6306 on seismic risk renewal in urban areas
laws.fullDescription: Turkish Law 6306/2012 on the Transformation of Areas Under Disaster Risk was enacted following the 2011 Van earthquake and gives authorities broad powers to demolish and rebuild structures deemed seismically risky. The law has been criticized for enabling gentrification and displacement of low-income communities in Istanbul under the guise of earthquake preparedness. The 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes (magnitude 7.7 and 7.6) killed over 50,000 people and revealed widespread non-compliance with building codes, with contractors subsequently criminally prosecuted. Post-earthquake legislation accelerated urban transformation with reduced owner consent thresholds.
laws.penalty: Continuing to occupy structures declared seismically risky: forced evacuation; non-compliant construction: criminal prosecution of developers and engineers
exceptions: Heritage listed buildings follow separate restoration procedures
Property owners who disagree with risk designation can request independent assessment
Compensation must be paid before forced demolition
laws.sourceLabel: Turkish Ministry of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change

quiz.q: Approximately how many people were killed in the February 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes in Turkey?
quiz.explanation: The February 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes (7.7 and 7.6 magnitude) killed over 50,000 people and exposed widespread non-compliance with building codes, leading to criminal prosecutions of contractors.

laws.title: Child Marriage and Early Marriage Restrictions
laws.subtitle: Ongoing legislative efforts to end under-18 marriage
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Civil Code technically sets the minimum marriage age at 17 (with parental consent) and 16 (with judicial approval), although the government pledged to raise the minimum to 18 without exceptions. Religious (imam) marriages without civil registration create a parallel system effectively allowing younger marriages not captured in official statistics. UNICEF estimates approximately 15% of Turkish girls are married before 18. Parliamentary debates on raising the age have been controversial, with some ruling party members arguing against removing judicial exceptions. A 2021 bill to fully ban child marriage failed to pass amid coalition tensions.
laws.penalty: Civil officers registering underage marriages: criminal charges; parents forcing marriage: up to 3 years imprisonment
exceptions: Judicial authorization currently permits marriage at 16 in exceptional circumstances
Previous religious marriages prior to reform receive transitional registration
Foreign marriages valid if legal in country of celebration
laws.sourceLabel: Turkish Ministry of Family and Social Services

quiz.q: According to UNICEF estimates, what percentage of Turkish girls are married before the age of 18?
quiz.explanation: UNICEF estimates approximately 15% of Turkish girls are married before age 18, driven partly by religious marriages without civil registration that circumvent legal age requirements.

laws.title: Istanbul Canal Project and Maritime Navigation Law
laws.subtitle: Proposed alternative to Bosphorus Strait
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Canal Istanbul project, announced in 2011 and approved by the Environment Ministry in 2021, plans a 45 km artificial waterway parallel to the Bosphorus connecting the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara. The project aims to create a commercially operated waterway outside the Montreux Convention (1936), which governs Bosphorus transit and gives Turkey control over warship passage. Critics argue bypassing Montreux could allow greater naval presence of non-Black Sea states. Environmental impact concerns involve disrupting Istanbul's water supply and displacing wetland ecosystems. Estimated cost exceeds $15 billion.
laws.penalty: Maritime violations in Turkish straits: substantial fines; unauthorized warship transit: diplomatic incidents and naval interception
exceptions: Montreux Convention guarantees free passage to commercial vessels
Black Sea riparian states have preferential warship transit rights
Scientific research vessels with notification rights
laws.sourceLabel: Turkish Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure

quiz.q: Which 1936 international treaty governs warship passage through the Bosphorus strait?
quiz.explanation: The Montreux Convention of 1936 gives Turkey control over Bosphorus Strait navigation, particularly governing warship passage and allowing Turkey to close the strait to belligerents during wartime.

laws.title: Cybercrime and Disinformation Law
laws.subtitle: Law 7418/2022 on spreading false information
laws.fullDescription: Turkey enacted Law 7418 in October 2022, adding Article 217/A to the Turkish Penal Code, criminalizing spreading 'false information' about the country's internal and external security, public order, or general health with intent to create fear or panic. The offense carries 1-3 years imprisonment, increased to 1.5-4.5 years if committed through press, and without possibility of suspension or deferred sentence. The Council of Europe Venice Commission criticized the law as incompatible with European freedom of expression standards, noting the vague definition of 'false information' enables selective prosecution of opposition voices and journalists.
laws.penalty: Spreading false information: 1-3 years imprisonment; if via media: 1.5-4.5 years; no suspension of sentence permitted
exceptions: Satire and clearly labeled opinion content has theoretical protection
Corrections published promptly may mitigate criminal exposure
Statements in parliamentary proceedings protected by immunity

quiz.q: What maximum sentence can Turkish journalists face for 'spreading false information' under Law 7418/2022?
quiz.explanation: Under Article 217/A added by Law 7418/2022, journalists spreading designated 'false information' via media face 1.5-4.5 years imprisonment with no possibility of suspended sentence.

laws.title: Foreign Exchange Obligation for Exporters
laws.subtitle: FX conversion requirements under Central Bank regulations
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Central Bank introduced mandatory foreign currency conversion requirements for exporters in 2022, initially requiring 25% then raised to 40% of export proceeds to be converted to Turkish lira within 180 days of receipt. The measure was intended to support lira liquidity and reduce dollarization during the currency crisis. The regulation, issued under Presidential Decree 4 and Central Bank communiqués, applies to export receipts above $25,000 and has been repeatedly adjusted. After the post-2023 election monetary policy normalization, conversion requirements were modified but the framework remains in place.
laws.penalty: Non-compliance with FX conversion: fines up to 10% of unconverted amount; repeated violations: suspension of export incentives
exceptions: Defense industry exporters exempt from conversion requirement
Strategic investment holders may retain full FX proceeds
Exporters in free trade zones follow separate FX rules
laws.sourceLabel: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey

quiz.q: What was the peak mandatory foreign currency conversion rate imposed on Turkish exporters in 2022?
quiz.explanation: Turkey raised the mandatory conversion of export foreign currency proceeds to Turkish lira to 40% in 2022, as part of measures to support lira liquidity during the currency crisis.

laws.title: Water Resources Law and Cross-Border Rivers
laws.subtitle: Turkish water law and Euphrates-Tigris basin disputes
laws.fullDescription: Turkey's Water Law (Law 167/1960) and subsequent regulations govern water resource management, with Turkey controlling headwaters of the Euphrates and Tigris rivers that flow through Syria and Iraq. Turkey's Southeastern Anatolia Project (GAP) involves 22 dams and 19 hydroelectric plants, significantly reducing downstream flows. International law on shared watercourses (UN Watercourses Convention 1997) has not been ratified by Turkey, Syria, or Iraq, leaving disputes unresolved by treaty. Water allocation has been a persistent source of regional tension, with Iraq accusing Turkey of reducing Tigris flows by up to 70% during low-rainfall periods.
laws.penalty: Unauthorized water extraction: administrative fines; industrial water pollution: criminal prosecution and remediation orders
exceptions: Agricultural water use from registered wells follows separate licensing
Municipal water utilities operate under separate regulatory framework
Emergency drought water restrictions override normal allocation rights

quiz.q: Which major infrastructure project controls Turkey's management of the Euphrates and Tigris headwaters?
quiz.explanation: The Southeastern Anatolia Project (GAP) with 22 dams and 19 hydroelectric plants gives Turkey effective control over Euphrates and Tigris headwaters, reducing flows to Syria and Iraq.

laws.title: EU-Turkey Accession Framework and Visa Liberalization
laws.subtitle: Suspended accession negotiations and customs union update
laws.fullDescription: Turkey has been an EU accession candidate since 1999, with membership negotiations formally opened in 2005 but effectively frozen since 2018 following European Parliament votes citing democratic backsliding. The EU-Turkey Customs Union (1995) covers industrial goods but excludes agriculture, services, and public procurement. Turkey has long sought an updated Customs Union extending to these sectors, while the EU conditions modernization on rule-of-law reforms. Turkish citizens face EU visa requirements despite a promised liberalization under the 2016 EU-Turkey Statement, with the EU citing Turkey's failure to meet all 72 benchmarks including anti-terrorism law reform.
laws.penalty: Illegal border crossing into EU from Turkey: criminal prosecution in destination country; Turkish nationals overstaying Schengen: deportation and multi-year entry ban
exceptions: Turkish workers with established rights under EEC-Turkey Association Agreement have preferential residency rights in some EU states
Diplomatic passport holders visa-free access continues
Turkish students at EU universities may use student visa pathway
laws.sourceLabel: Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs EU Directorate

quiz.q: In what year did Turkey formally open EU membership negotiations?
quiz.explanation: Turkey formally opened EU membership accession negotiations in 2005, six years after being accepted as a candidate country in 1999, though negotiations are effectively frozen since 2018.
